Reborn: Apocalypse - Volume 4



(A LitRPG/Wuxia Story)




L M Kerr

Prologue



“Focus… fire!” A loud command echoed out into the air, quickly followed by a series of rippling explosions.

The speaker, an Asian man dressed in black pants and a dark grey vest, crossed his arms as he watched. He tapped his right foot impatiently, black socks melding with the thin, black sandals he wore.

In front of him were a series of smoking craters five meters abreast. The man studied each crater, his face expressionless. The air gradually began to clear after a few seconds, revealing the surroundings.

This all was taking place in the midst of a Magic Forest, in a large clearing hidden inside its depths.

There were ten other figures in the area, spread out in an even line about 10 meters opposite the speaker. These ten warriors were dressed in masks and armor, keeping their identities secret even as they trained.

If Micheal had been present, he would've instantly recognized these warriors as members of the Beasts of Providence. Their gear setup was identical to the warriors of the Division he had fought against.

The only real difference was the fact that, instead of bearing an animal’s visage, each warrior had the image of yellow rippling flames stained on their masks.

Red and yellow balls of fire began to flutter into the air, rising above the hands of the ten masked warriors. This fire pulsated in small globes, burning quietly as they spawned.

The Asian speaker looked up as he finished studying each crater, his face still impassive. He had short black hair and grey eyes, his calm attitude matching his rather unexciting features.

The non-masked warrior began to speak again.

“Remember.” He began, gesturing to the ten warriors,

“Condense your power. Three meters wide is your goal for this month. Five meters is too weak.” The speaker went on to explain this concept in detail.

When fighting supernaturally powerful enemies, certain facts had to be recognized. In particular: an explosion that would kill a normal human on Earth might only startle a Mid-Tier Magic Beast on the Second Layer.

The speaker's words urged them to focus their attacks into a smaller area. This would increase the intensity and deadliness of each explosion, trading off range for immediate power.

The ten masked warriors all quietly nodded after the man finished his explanation. Several of them began to sit down as they meditated, focusing on the red fireballs that hovered above them. Others remained standing or walked out into the forest, also meditating, but in their own way.

The speaker smiled slightly when he saw this. He was just about to add something else when he came to an abrupt pause.

“Oh?” For a few split seconds, he stood still. His eyes flickered as he looked into the distance, focusing on something that wasn’t visible.

Right after that…

He tapped on a Mid-Tier Spatial Ring that adorned his right hand.

A mask appeared in that same hand. Like the masks of the other warriors, this one was stained with the image of fire. What set it apart, however, was the fact that its flames were a deep blue instead of yellow.

In one smooth motion, the speaker put the mask on, hiding his features as he stood straight. A long, black robe appeared around his body, covering the rest of him.

A heartbeat later…

Dark blue fire exploded out from his body, enshrouding him in just seconds. These flames cindered the earth itself, turning nearby grass to ash and cracking the ground beneath. They burned with horrific strength, so brutally hot the air itself seemed to writhe against them.

As soon as the fire formed, the speaker shot up towards the sky. He left a fading trail of blue flames behind him, rocketing out of the clearing in just seconds.

The meditating warriors all looked up in surprise as they watched their instructor vanish.

Gradually, as the speaker soared up, the large clearing his trainees were standing in seemed to shrink down in size. The figures of the ten warriors inside grew small alongside it.

As the instructor flew, the surrounding area became more clear. Thousands of trees dotted his sight, spread between several other large clearings.

Within each of those new clearings stood similar-sized groups, one large group of trainees and one instructor, all masked. The decoration of each mask varied from person to person, group to group. Some bore the image of various animals, from wild boars to mountain lions, while others held images of flames, clouds, or other non-living things.

Tens of new humans had come into view, across five clearings.

The speaker flew higher.

Tens turned into hundreds, five clearings turned into fifty.

He flew even higher.

Hundreds turned into thousands, fifty clearings turned into more than 300.

By the time the speaker had reached the highest point of his flight, more than 6,000 men and women could be seen, a hidden army of warriors training in the depths of a large Magic Forest, spread across hundreds of man-made clearings.

Finally, the blue flame-masked warrior rapidly began to fall down. His body shifted to hurtle towards the ground, shooting like an arrow. He fell directly towards one clearing in particular, the largest one in sight.

Despite the size of the clearing, the only thing within it was a large stone table and several chairs.

Even while falling from several hundred meters in the air, crashing down at breakneck speed, the original speaker could tell that most of those chairs were occupied. 12 distinct figures were seated around the table currently, leaving only three spots free.

In the blink of an eye, the falling warrior fell until he was only a dozen meters above the ground. He was a mere split second away from finding himself smashed into bits, about ten meters from the stone table, when the man finally acted.

The blue flames that surrounded his body grew a little darker. The flames under his feet grew slightly more intense.

Then…

A tiny explosion blasted out, just below the man's feet.

Boiling blue fire cascaded in the air, transmitting the full force of the man’s fall into a powerful attack. This explosive strike did not spread out far, however.

It didn't expand to five meters, or four, or even three.

Instead, it spread to about half the size of a clenched fist, a deadly explosion that appeared and then vanished almost instantly, as if it had never been.

“Slow as always, Blue Flame.” One of the seated warriors spoke out loud as Blue Flame landed softly on the ground, grumbling at the late arrival.

Like Blue Flame, and the rest of the warriors at the table, this man wore a long black robe and a mask that hid his features. On his particular mask, an image of fractured earth and jutting stone could be seen. When this man spoke, the table itself seemed to... rumble.

“My apologies, Rupture. I moved as soon as I was informed.” The commanding tone that had colored Blue Flame’s voice when he was teaching had vanished, replaced with placid calm.

“It’s fine.” A new voice interjected itself into the conversation, cutting everyone off. This voice wasn’t a particularly imposing one, yet nevertheless drew everyone’s attention down to one end of the stone table.

On it, a warrior sat by himself, his mask adorned with the visage of a Praying Mantis.

“Lord Mantis.” Blue Flame bowed his head respectfully as he took a seat. His eyes flicked to the right and left, noting the two empty spots that were left. He spotted several familiar masks, from one holding a picture of a large storm cloud, to one painted with a silver sword, to one that held an image of an albino tree.

Every single person around this table had a unique mask. More than that, however…

They all gave off incredibly keen sensations of danger. Even the weakest person here was a strong First Rate Warrior, still in the midst of growing stronger.

These were the strongest hidden elites of humanity on the Second Layer, warriors that the Vile King had personally paid close attention to.

The King Division.

“Everyone’s here, we will begin immediately.” Mantis replied, waving at Blue Flame casually.

“This meeting of the King Division has been called because of some... difficulties… that I have encountered.” Mantis’ voice carried a hint of begrudging irritation.

“Difficulties?” A female warrior, wearing a mask that bore an image of a golden snake, broke in with a question. Her words carried a ferocious force of presence, impossible to ignore.

“Yes, Sun Snake.” Mantis returned, his voice cool as he ignored the rather imposing pressure the woman gave off,

“Sansa is dead.”

“Hah! She certainly had that coming. A jack-of-all will always be a master-of-none.” Sun Snake’s voice held a hint of mirth, showing no compassion at the loss of one of her allies.

The rest of the table stiffened up as they heard the news, intense stares drilling into Mantis.

“She died…? How?” Storm, a man bearing a mask covered in storm clouds, broke in, his tone questioning. As he spoke, the air around him seemed to stir, his words alone seeming to summon the wind.

“Yes, she is dead. I’ll explain it all in detail later.” Mantis sighed,

“For now, though, she must be replaced. Rex is strong and my role as Lux is centralizing, but it's not enough.” Mantis began, waving at one of the two empty seats,

“We’ll need to take full control of the Syndicates. Not only must Sansa be replaced, but it's also time we removed and replaced Fortuna as well.” His voice took on a harsh edge as he looked around the table.

“You all know the rules. Everyone here is mighty, but that is only by the grace of him, the King Above.” Mantis sternly studied each warrior present, his gaze roaming to them, one by one,

“Only those that have accepted a Mind Root can appear in public.”

The Beast King paused for a few seconds before folding his hands together.

“So, now, we must decide…”

“Who among us will become humanity’s next Baro-" Abruptly, Mantis' words were cut off. For a split second, his eyes glazed over.

In that same moment, the eyes of every single member of the King Division froze in unison, all emotion vanishing from their faces.

It was an eerie, unsettling scene... as if someone had grabbed tight the strings of a group of puppets, freezing them in place.

The moment passed.

Mantis' vision cleared as he glanced around the table, shaking his head.

"Disregard what I previously said." The Beast King said, his voice taking on a harsh edge.

As he spoke, Mantis turned his gaze to the outer edges of the clearing and then upward, towards the sky above.

For the briefest moment, Mantis' eyes caught sight of the flickering wings of a small, pale blue butterfly.

"There's been a change of plans."

.

Chapter 1



-

“What does it all mean..?”

The speaker of those words sat alone, by himself, in a brightly lit room, resting upon a large, carved wooden chair.

He was a large man, a Byren warrior, one of the natives of the Second Layer. He had a well-weathered appearance with a large, white beard and a tan, lined face that looked slightly at odds with his bulky, muscular body. He was dressed in a simple white robe with a black, diagonal stitching line that stretched from his right shoulder to his left hip.

Before this man rested a large wooden table, strewn with colorful maps, long, tidy reports, and several large notebooks covered in scribbles and notes. The edges of the room were lined with bookcases that filled to the brim with books, lit by several small, glowing crystal rocks that were built into the ceiling.

“Humans, Farians, Orkal, and Rakkonians.” The man spoke aloud, his voice gruff and calm. With each Race he named, he tapped on four different locations on one of the large maps in front of him.

“Four different worlds connected to one… a bridge between space and time like I’ve only ever seen once before.” A brief flash of darkness appeared in the powerful Byren’s sharp green eyes.

“Patience. I’ve waited 800 years for this opportunity… I will not squander it.” The dark light vanished, replaced by a gleam of cool, cold logic as the man took a deep breath.

The man turned his attention back towards the map in front of him.

“The Orkals have been enslaved. The Rakkonians have been split apart and will fall within a matter of weeks. The Farians are stable, but will collapse once their Lord Justiciar is dealt with.” Race by Race, the man marked each one down, before pausing over an area outlined on the eastern portion of the map.

“Only the Humans have proven troublesome.” He murmured, donning a small frown.

“The Syndicates and their City-Camps pose little threat… it’s those rat-like Beasts of Providence… they scurry around and hide like cockroaches, yet somehow manage to interfere with my plans at every step.”

“But now… something is different.” The Byren warrior tapped his scarred fingers on the map, his frown deepening.

“10 days have passed with no sign of them… why? What are they planning?” The man traced his finger along the eastern portion of the map, up to the territory of the Dragon Mountains.

“The undead Drake haunting these mountains has become more active of late, but that can’t be it.” The man’s finger rose further, before landing squarely on the area occupied by the Farians, the Woolen Forest.

“Now that I think about it, the massive explosion that erupted here also took place 10 days ago.” His eyes narrowed sharply, like the gaze of a hawk zeroing in on its prey.

“Is it related? Perhaps. But how? Why?” The Byren took a few seconds to stare at the map, his gaze relentless, before letting out a deep sigh.

“There is so much I do not know…” He shook his head after a few moments.

“Their silence is unsettling, but in the end, I suppose I don’t have a choice.”

The man slowly rose to his feet and walked over to an ornate stone door.

“This is the best chance I’ll have to conquer the Sanctum. Everything will be decided then.”

The Byren opened the door and left the room.

Outside was a large valley. The study he’d just left was built into the side of a large mountain, a small, secure hut hidden away in the midst of a large mountain range.

The bearded Byren moved over to the side, resting his left hand upon a thick, heavily scarred portion of rock wall. The stone here was blackened and covered in cracks, imprinted with hundreds upon thousands of fist indentions. This type of scarring repeated itself for thousands of meters, up and down this large gray mountain, giving the air an old, smoky feel.

In the same moment, as the old warrior placed his hand on the wall, his arm began to tremble.

The man sighed as he saw this, grasping his shaking left arm with his right hand, holding it still.

“800 years of practice and training have taken their toll.” The Byren muttered, watching as now both of his hands trembled against his will.

“What did those humans call it? Incurable arthritis?” He smiled grimly.

“The pangs of a corporeal body.”

The warrior chuckled to himself quietly before turning his gaze off to the side, his smile fading.

The rest of the valley was like a scene from a warzone.

The ground was littered with enormous gashes in the earth, torn and ripped up stone shuttering upward at sharp angles. Large slabs of bedrock could be seen, jutting out of the side of the valley, covered in cracks and cuts.

The valley was like bleeding sore upon the earth itself, a devastated landscape where nothing could survive.

And, finally, the Byren shifted his eyes towards the center of the valley, where rested the blackened skulls of several dead Dragons, the remains of more than a dozen Blue Drakes, fallen in battle centuries ago.

“The Dragons are dead. The Dark Wraiths nigh annihilated. And the Torens have left, abandoning the Ancient Realm after they won the war.” The warrior spoke aloud, his voice cold and emotionless.

“Perhaps they thought this land a dead one, the past forgotten to time, history erased.” His voice grew harsher.

“But I have not forgotten. I will never forget.”

“I will do whatever it takes...”

“Even if I must become a Deity myself.”

Orion Thunderfist, the First Lord, and Supreme Commander of the Divine Might Sect clenched his fists, a shockwave of lightning blasting out into the air around him.

“Maria… I will avenge you.”

.

Chapter 2



--

"He didn’t drop any Points?” Director Prime frowned as he looked down at a mangled dead body.

The corpse was smashed to unrecognizable bits of flesh, blood, and bone. Whatever it used to be should be dead, though Prime found little solace in that observation. He was all too familiar with supposedly dead enemies coming back to life.

Prime’s own body was hardly in better condition. His arms, legs, and chest bore more than a dozen knuckle-sized holes, pierced clean through, that he had just bandaged up. Almost miraculously, none of these injuries had damaged important organs, tendons, or blood vessels, but they were still serious wounds nevertheless.

“Hmm.” Prime sat down next to the body as he began to study it, his entire demeanor calm and unhurried.

The former S Ranker, and the dead body next to him, were both sitting in the middle of a large crater, the remnants of a once-proud mountain shattered by explosive battle. Bits of debris and rock floated in mid-air, frozen in the midst of flying outward. The sky above was overcast and dark, giving the crater a rather dreary atmosphere.

Time itself stood still for Prime as he drew upon his World Matrix Type Ability, assessing what had just taken place.

“No Points, yet he’s dead… it’s impossible he’s a new arrival.” Prime paused, his eyes boring into the dead body.

Several minutes passed in silence as Prime sat there, simply thinking. He continued to remain still as he carefully broke down everything he had observed. Then, he physically dissected the corpse in great detail, confirming he hadn't managed to preserve its brain while also searching for anything that might matter. After that, he scanned the nearby area for anything it may have dropped, manually scattering dust and cutting into rock.

Finally, after all of that… he repeated these same actions for a second time, but in even more excruciating detail. Anything he changed would revert back to normal once time resumed, meaning there was no need to be careful.

In this frozen world of time, a full 3 hours passed before Prime finished this investigation.

Most would consider that an absurd amount of time given how little there was to investigate. Prime’s exquisite search of the nearby area alone took up a full 45 minutes of that time, doubled because he did it twice.

It was mind-numbingly boring… but it was the norm for Prime.

After all, while the Director was 34 years old in terms of physical age…

Mentally, Prime had now lived for a bit more than 108 years.

That discrepancy of 74 years arose because of how often Prime stopped time.

The average human was awake, thinking and moving, for 14-16 hours of the day. After reaching Sky Tier, that number jumped to around 20 hours.

Prime, on the other hand, usually found himself awake for at least 100 hours every day, oftentimes much longer. When time was stopped, his body didn’t weaken and his energy expenditure was minute. With his strong Soul stat, the main thing limiting how long he could freeze time was his mental willpower.

Over the course of the past day alone, Prime had been awake for 815 hours, or roughly 34 days. Most of that time was spent thinking, planning, and examining his surroundings or enemies in the midst of battle. In combat, he froze time repeatedly, oftentimes for multiple instances each second, to carefully plan his movements and avoid any surprises.

“He was definitely my target. He was strong… but not strong enough.” Prime nodded as he reached a couple of conclusions.

“So… a Deathless Clone, with some type of mind-enhancing Ability.”

After considering all the possible options, given the information he did know, it was the only thing that seemed likely.

There were several Abilities in the Shop that granted a person the power to spawn a ‘Clone,’ a copy of oneself that would obey your commands. The range, intelligence, and power of these Clones varied greatly, and all of them possessed some type of downside.

The Deathless Clone Ability that Prime was referencing allowed one to create multiple realistic Clones, but split the user’s overall power as a result, weakening the main body. Its other downside, one shared by most Clone Abilities, was that the farther each Clone was from the main body, the weaker that Clone’s memory became.

Prime sighed as he looked at the dead body once more, his mouth twisting. Here, where no one could see him, he hunched his shoulders and sat down, exhaustion appearing on his face.

He…

He was tired.

Really tired.

These past few years… no, these past few decades had been exhausting.

It all started back when he was Chosen in the First Wave.

When he arrived on the First Layer, he had been equal parts shocked and horrified at what he found. This foreign world was like a place out of nightmare, full of violence and terror.

He had started with a pitifully small number of Points: 6,000. It was barely enough to purchase an Ability, forcing him to choose the inexpensive Mortal Tier Ki Cultivation Ability, something that ended up being a blessing in disguise.

From there… his story was not that special, not at first.

He fought to live alongside the people he arrived with. Despite his slow start, Prime quickly adapted to the environment, doing his best to protect his new companions. He overcame his fears, knowing that his new allies were depending on him, and grew into a strong leader.

At his core, Prime had always been obsessively methodical in everything he did.

Because of that, his group of survivors weathered storms of Morenkai with ease. Even when they encountered a group of Abnormal Morenkai, everyone survived because of his efforts.

Time passed and the number of people he led grew, forming a large survivor’s colony that was focused on farming Morenkai for Points. He didn’t give up on exploring, especially after the Great Bridge appeared and connected their Cluster to the Main Cluster… but his primary focus was on building the strength of his colony. Their survival was most important.

Everything seemed to be going well… until 4 months in, one month after the Great Bridge appeared.

The peace of his colony collapsed as they were attacked, not by Morenkai, but by humans.

Specifically, a single human.

A serial killer that owned the incredibly rare Void Ripper Type Ability.

It was a Limited Ability that could be bought only 10 times. It had been completely bought out by the time Prime glanced at it, priced at 40,000 Points.

That price was relatively inexpensive… but that didn’t mean the Ability was weak. More Points typically meant a stronger Ability, but this wasn’t always true.

As Prime came to personally learn, the Void Ripper Type was incredibly powerful.

It gifted their attacker with skin that was absurdly thick, blocking bullets like they were paintballs. It made this murderer far stronger than Prime’s team, giving the man the power to literally rip apart steel with his bare hands.

Prime had prepared half a dozen countermeasures to protect his survival colony. After four months of survival, he had long since outgrown any naivety he might have possessed. He was well aware that they could be attacked at any moment, by Morenkai or fellow humans.

He had thought he was ready…

And he was wrong.

Nothing worked against this butcher. Every trap Prime had readied, every weapon he launched, every Ability his allies pulled out…

All of them failed. The butcher came, killed, and then left.

On the day before his group was attacked, there had been 1,012 living members in his colony.

On the day after, there were 907 survivors.

A single man had killed over 100 people, men and women that Prime had promised he would protect.

It was a horrific experience for the Director. It showed Prime how numbers could mean nothing and how weapons could become meaningless. His mindset began to shift, his view of the world becoming distinctly colder. He realized, then, that when push came to shove, only one thing really mattered.

Power.

After that fateful day, Prime spent a large amount of time pouring through the Shop. He ramped his methodical nature up to the maximum, using every waking moment to plan, to think, and to research.

About two days after his colony was attacked, he finally decided on his Type Ability.

The World Matrix Type cost 82,950 Points, a significant investment to make on the First Layer. Its description spelled out its sole power to freeze time for everyone, as well as how it did almost nothing for a person’s stats. To most people, it was a very mediocre Type Ability. Other Type Abilities offered more direct benefits, ranging from mystical powers to enhanced stats.

In Prime’s eyes, however, this Type Ability exceeded all others.

It gave him the one resource he never had enough of: Time.

After he obtained the Ability, Prime began to flourish.

The efficiency of his colony skyrocketed. His plans became incredibly deep and thorough. His own power jumped enormously.

And so, around three weeks later, when the man with the Void Ripper Ability attacked again, the number of deaths dropped drastically.

More than 100 survivors had died in the first attack. In the second attack, however…

Only a single person died.

And that was the butcher himself, killed by Prime’s own hand.

Prime sighed for a second time as these old memories rose up. He smiled a little sadly as he ran his fingers through his golden hair.

“What does it all mean?” He looked at the body, his surroundings, and the situation as a whole…

And then he pursed his lips as he started to think, trying his best to understand what was happening here.

The Director was widely considered a genius. His enemies, his subordinates, even those that hated him agreed on that.

Prime felt that he was probably the only person alive that disagreed with that assessment.

He knew his limits.

He was no genius.

He was not a person that could come up with a diabolic countermeasure on the spot. He couldn’t see through a person’s words as they spoke them or judge a plan’s value from his intuition. He was not a rapid thinker that could split his focus multiple ways at the same time.

What he could do, however, was spend inordinate amounts of time to make up for that.

A plan that might take a genius 5 minutes to come up with could take Prime 5 hours to realize. Insight that would come to a rare prodigy in mere seconds might take Prime several days of deep thought. A situation that a top planner might need a day or two to breakdown could take Prime half a month.

The only thing that mattered to Prime was that he achieved his goals. How long it took him meant nothing to him. Loneliness and tedium that would drive other humans insane was merely a normal part of his life.

An hour passed as Prime sat by himself, simply thinking.

And then another.

And another.

And…

7 hours after Prime sat down to think, he stood back up, voicing a conclusion.

“I need more information.” He didn’t know what all he was missing, but he realized now that there was still too much he did not know. More thinking would not solve his problem, though he would think things over again later, just to be certain.

Reality returned to normal around Prime as time resumed. Debris that had been flung into the air settled. Dirt finished falling to the floor and a cool breeze picked up and brushed past him.

The Director winced as he touched a few spots on his body with a grimace. When time was frozen, the pain his body remained consistent, making it easier to ignore. After time was restored, that pain began to twist, jumping back with a vengeance.

Prime stored the corpse of the dead Clone in his Spatial Ring. He then walked a dozen meters over to one specific spot within this crater.

A small grey dagger appeared in his right hand. He used this to stab into the earth and ripped out several chunks of it. Several seconds passed as he focused on this.

Finally, with a grunt, Prime stored the dagger and reached into the hole he had created.

From within it, he pulled out a pile of broken metal, the remnants of several shattered Spatial Rings. He stored these shards in his own Spatial Ring, choosing to leave behind nothing that had the potential to be a clue, however minor.

As he finished storing these bits of metal and was preparing to move out… something rather unexpected happened.

A battle started to break out.

Prime’s eyes whipped to the north.

Within the Woolen Forest, many miles away from him, he could sense a large number of powerful beings start to clash. Explosions of energy rocked the air, bringing flashes of light that were visible from far away.

“What in the world…?” Prime looked off into the distance with a frown.

Without hesitation, he froze time once more.

These energy undulations and explosions had to be from the High-Tier Magic Beasts that were supposed to be ambushing the Farian Life Festival. For some reason, they had begun to fight each other.

“Is it because I killed the Clone? Even if he was the leader, that shouldn’t be right…” Prime muttered to himself as he looked down at his Spatial Ring. He then scratched his head.

After Prime had arrived on the Second Layer, he had immediately begun to investigate the existence of the Vile King. The Director had analyzed what Micheal told him more than a hundred times, internalizing the rage he felt over the death of his closest subordinates as he sought out the truth.

It took only a single day for Prime to believe Micheal. Technically, Prime spent more than 2 weeks thinking things over, but physically, it only took a single day.

Once Prime realized the Vile King did exist, he started to cautiously hunt down the man’s subordinates with a vengeance. Prime had not forgiven Micheal, but the Vile King’s existence was far more intolerable and became Prime’s main priority. The deaths of his men came about because of that man’s arrogant manipulations.

One thing led to another and Prime eventually discovered that this attack was going to happen. He swiftly decided to intervene, intent on taking out some Seeds that were higher up the food chain.

Prime continued to watch the battle between High-Tier Magic Beasts from a distance, unfreezing time. He didn’t make any other active decision, opting to simply observe for now.

His target had always been the leadership behind this attack. The grunts carrying it out were bound to be disposable. Even if he brought their corpses to a Byren Deathreader, he would probably get nothing useful. The higher-ups were the ones that would have valuable intel.

He didn’t have anything against the Farians, but he also wasn’t here to babysit them. Protecting them would have meant giving his targets time to escape.

He was pleased to see the attack fail… but he couldn’t help but to be confused at why.

He was even more confused when, some moments later, a gargantuan explosion tore into existence, obliterating a massive chunk of forest with searing flames, followed almost immediately by a hefty shockwave.

It was an awe-inspiring sight. He had never seen such a clear display of power, an explosion that rivaled small nuclear explosions on Earth.

Prime spent a few hours trying to analyze what he had seen from afar before eventually deciding on his next course of action.

He needed to investigate in person, before the Farians realized the Life Festival wasn’t being attacked and sent a team over.

Prime sprinted down from his mountain, drawing on his Draconic Blood to drastically boost his regeneration, strength, and speed. He could only use the blood’s power in limited amounts each day, and while he had used this blood extensively in his fight against Mantis, he still had some left in reserve.

Obtaining this Draconic Blood was one of the improvements Prime had made in his past few weeks here on the Second Layer, a change to a new stat in his Status, his ‘Physique,’ that he’d obtained from completing a rather strenuous Inheritance. No matter how focused he was on tracking down his enemies, he would never forget the importance of power. He was always seeking out ways to enhance his strength.

Prime moved through the southern part of the Woolen Forest at great speed. It took him a relatively brief amount of time to reach the place where the explosion had originated. Once he arrived, he approached the epicenter carefully, freezing time repeatedly to scout out his surroundings.

Not surprisingly, he found himself in another crater, this one significantly larger than the one he started in. The ground had been blasted black by the explosion, burnt to a crisp. The thousands of trees that had existed here were gone, annihilated into ash. Most of the earth had been flattened.

The bits that had not been flattened, however, were what came to interest Prime the most.

“Huh.” After freezing time again, Prime knelt down next to one of the clumps and ran a hand down its side. The black lump had fused with the ground and become mostly immovable.

He spent a long period carefully slicing into this black lump, eventually realizing what it was.

The corpse of a High-Tier Magic Beast, burnt almost beyond recognization. He checked several other lumps, confirming that they were the same. He also noted that all of them were missing their Spirit Crystals.

“The explosion killed them…? Who did this? How?” It was a startling realization.

High-Tier Magic Beasts were extremely sturdy. Killing one was difficult.

Killing several of them at the same time was insanely hard. He had experienced that difficulty firsthand inside the Inheritance that held his Draconic Blood. One of the trials he’d had to complete involved several battles against a number of High-Tier creatures, some at the same time. He beat each trial, in the end, but only by the skin of his teeth.

No normal explosion was enough to cause this.

A few minutes passed in real-time as Prime moved about the crater, investigating the scene. He left the High-Tier Magic Beast corpses where they lay, though only because he had no choice. All of the corpses were fused with the ground and would take far too much time to remove.

The explosion had destroyed almost everything in the vicinity. Nevertheless, Prime persevered, methodically spending enormous amounts of time as he dug up large tracts of earth.

Because of that, he managed to find a small, fist-sized spike that had escaped destruction, buried a meter beneath the cindered earth.

And, shortly after that, he found something else…

Or, rather, something else found him.

“I thought I smelled a familiar stench.” A deep voice rumbled into the air while Prime was in the midst of sprinting to a new section of the crater.

Immediately, Prime froze time. A short while later, he unfroze it as he realized that the speaker was out of his range. When time was frozen, he could move around freely, but only in a limited area. Anything beyond a certain range was something he couldn’t see or interact with.

Around a hundred and twenty meters to the south, Prime could make out the speaker walking towards him. It appeared to be…

‘A talking monkey..?’ Prime blinked, temporarily at a loss.

‘No, it’s a gorilla. A Transformation Type user?’ Prime clarified his thought a moment later, his eyes going cold as he looked at the armor the creature was wearing.

The gear was damaged, but still obviously the same type of armor that the warriors of the Beasts of Providence used.

‘An enemy.’

“I’m surprised the lackeys of the Drakes aren’t extinct yet. Your masters died out long ago, runt.” The Transformation Type user’s voice echoed out in the air as he took several confident steps forward.

Prime missed none of this, his gaze calmly boring into the warrior. Prime was well aware he was in no condition to fight. He had used up 90% of the Draconic Blood he could draw on, while his energy stores were at dangerous lows. He took those things into account as he began to prepare himself, knowing he might not have a choice.

“I have no master, man or Drake. Who are you?” Prime returned, putting up a confident, collected facade as he began to walk towards the other warrior.

Unlike most of his other targets, this one was talking an unusual amount, something that made Prime wary. He decided to try to take advantage of the man’s chattiness and see if he could gain some free information.

“Who am I?” The talking gorilla paused before continuing,

“Yvvtal the Destroyer, of course.” An almost tangible wave of killing intent began to flow from the man's body,

“I’m back… and…” The warrior donned a blood-curdling smile,

“I’m here to destroy.”

.

Chapter 3



.

A cool breeze swept through a large stone canyon, fluttering freely as it flew across cracked brown rocks and soared above wide jutting boulders. This wind crossed the 500-meter gap from one wall to the other, floating above the meandering river that guided the canyon’s path.

Warm sunlight shined down on this canyon from above, giving it a rather cheerful appearance that was decidedly at odds with its grim name: the Dark Canyon.

Located at the southern border of the Divine Might Sect’s territory, the Dark Canyon stretched for hundreds of miles. Just like how the Dragon Mountains served as a natural barrier against the Silent Sword Sect to the north, the Dark Canyon served as a boundary for the Ground Demon Sect to the south.

At first glance, it seemed to be far less effective of a barrier. The Dark Canyon stood only a half dozen miles thick at its widest, while the Dragon Mountains sat between 100 and 200 miles throughout. In that aspect alone, regardless of how long the canyon was, the two sites were incomparable.

Nevertheless, it was common knowledge that the Dark Canyon was significantly more dangerous to cross.

Shin kept all of that in mind as he took a deep breath and then exhaled, his gaze never wavering as he stared down a long scope.

The blonde-haired man was perched precariously on the side of a canyon wall, resting on a ledge that jutted out merely half a meter. He was dressed in a set of faded brown pants and a dull brown shirt, camouflaging himself against the brown stone walls.

In Shin’s hands was a long, silver rifle inlaid with various blue symbols. He held it with a sense of familiarity and practice, two fingers resting on its trigger while he aimed down its scope.

“Careful now…” Shin muttered as he adjusted the long gun slightly, focusing on his target.

Around 350 meters in front of Shin, strolling along the rocky canyon floor, a dark, humanoid shadow could be seen. This creature had two arms and legs, a torso and a head, many of the normal features of a human… but not all of them.

Instead of possessing a mouth, eyes, or nose, the shadow’s face was eerily blank. It was like a mannequin, having a body that appeared normal at a distance, but lacking the true essence of a human.

Shin breathed in.

Shin exhaled.

The shadow continued to move. It might not possess any eyes, but the creature picked its path carefully, walking without hesitation.

It didn’t seem to be aware of Shin, but… it just so happened to be walking directly towards him.

Shin raised his gun ever so slightly, a small bead of sweat forming along his cheek. He made several small adjustments as the shadow continued moving, keeping track of things like the distance, the breeze, and anything else that might matter.

Seconds slipped by.

The shadow kept walking, closing the gap between it and Shin by 50 meters.

Shin breathed in.

Shin exhaled.

The bead of sweat that had formed continued to travel down his cheek, stopping only after it reached the edge of his chin.

In that time, Shin’s hands tightened, shifting his rifle by a few millimeters.

The shadow never stopped moving, now only 250 meters distant.

Shin breathed in.

Shin exhaled.

The drop of sweat fell from his face, dripping lightly onto the rocky ledge.

Shin’s eyes twitched.

The shadow abruptly froze, its faceless head jerking to point at Shin.

For a tiny, split-second, nothing happened.

A moment later…

Shin pulled the trigger.

‘Expand.’

A small, silver bullet silently blasted from Shin’s gun. As soon as it emerged, it rapidly began to swell up in size. It went from being the length of Shin’s middle finger to around the size of a skateboard in a fraction of a second.

That bullet ripped through the air lightning-fast, flying forth in a blur. It crossed the distance between Shin and the shadow so quickly it seemed like it should have been impossible to notice.

Nevertheless, somehow, the shadow reacted.

Its dark body twisted as it lurched a step to the right. The creature actually took this step before Shin even pulled the trigger on his gun. Despite the large distance between the two, the shadow had immediately sensed when Shin was about to kill it, allowing it to preemptively dodge.

Unfortunately for the shadow, that didn’t matter.

Shin’s silver bullet, in mid-flight, adjusted its trajectory. Instead of blasting forward towards Shin’s original target, the space where the shadow should’ve been standing, it landed one step to the right…

Exactly where the shadow had dodged to.

The huge bullet slammed into the shadow’s chest and obliterated it, a flash of silver light searing out. It travelled clean through the shadow and pierced into the ground behind it, sending up a storm of stone shrapnel and shattered rock.

The shadow collapsed, its body caving in as it fell apart. Its corpse dissipated as it vanished from existence, all remnants of it fading away.

Just like that, the shadow was gone.

“About freakin’ time.” Shin lowered his rifle, heaving a huge sigh of relief as tension vanished from his shoulders. He took several steadying breaths as he got to his feet, a small smile appearing on his face.

A moment later, Shin vanished as he teleported away from his ledge.

Instead of inspecting the spot where the shadow had died, Shin moved in the opposite direction. He spent the next several seconds teleporting over and over, speeding through the canyon.

It was only after he crossed through thousands of meters that Shin finally came to a stop, landing atop a large stone pillar in the middle of a barren stretch within the Dark Canyon.

“Welcome back, Shin. How’d it go?” A woman’s voice greeted Shin moments after he appeared.

“Yo, Sofa.” Shin smiled a little wider as he glanced at the speaker.

A brown-haired woman sat on the rocky ground, leaning her back against a small stone boulder. She was dressed in a plain brown dress and brown boots, her eyes shut tight in meditation. Two grey shortswords rested in her lap, covered with a hint of red energy.

“The Shadow Seeker’s dead! My Soul Rifle’s working great.” Shin patted his rifle affectionately.

That long-ranged Artifact weapon was very similar to the Soul Pistol he’d obtained on the First Layer. Just like his Soul Pistol, it was capable of firing most types of bullets and allowed him to guide them as they shot forward, adjusting their trajectories.

The main difference between the two was that this gun was stronger and more precise, able to shoot farther and with more accuracy. His Soul Pistol had cost him 26,500 Points while this rifle cost about three times that, Points well spent in his eyes.

“Did anything change?” Sophia kept her eyes shut as she responded, remaining in her meditative pose.

Shin stretched his right arm while Sophia spoke, sitting down shortly after. He stretched his left arm in the same motion, though simply out of habit. That arm looked like a normal arm, but was actually a metallic Melding Plate Arm, an Artifact he’d used to replace his left arm after he’d lost it in battle on the First Layer.

Shin dangled his legs off the edge of the stone pillar as he replied, “Yeah! This time, it tried to dodge before I even attacked!” Shin’s voice held a hint of excitement.

When Sophia heard this, she finally opened her eyes. Her pupils glowing pink in the afternoon light, shining eerily.

“Perhaps it sensed your killing intent?” Sophia smiled as she began to get to her feet,

“Either way, it sounds strong enough to be useful inside the First Gate.”

If what Micheal had shared with them was accurate, the First Gate found inside the Soul King’s Inheritance was an incredible training aid.

Shin grinned back at Sophia, clenching his fists as he nodded in agreement.

They could finally leave this hellish place.

Before Micheal left the First Layer, he had sent Shin and Sophia a detailed message outlining his plan for them. Most of that plan centered around the Soul King’s Inheritance, a famous tomb located within the Dark Canyon, roughly 40 miles from Shin and Sophia’s current location.

According to Micheal, for the plan to work, they needed to camp within the Dark Canyon for several days first, something no sane inhabitant of the Second Layer would do.

It was an unusual idea, to put it lightly. The Dark Canyon was considered an extremely dangerous place for good reason: the existence of the Shadow Seekers.

The Dark Canyon was not inhabited by any living thing. It was like a barren desert, devoid of life.

The shadowy humanoid that Shin had killed earlier, a Shadow Seeker, was not a living creature. In fact, it did not even exist in the Dark Canyon normally.

They only came into existence when a living being stepped into the territory of the Dark Canyon, with a singular purpose: To hunt.

Each Shadow Seeker was different. The magical beings mimicked the appearance of their targets. In terms of power, Micheal had claimed the first Shadow Seeker they would encounter would be roughly as strong as they were.

They found this out for themselves five days ago, right after Shin and Sophia started camping in the canyon, and seven days after they arrived on the Second Layer. The unnerving creatures had shown up out of nowhere, moving in to attack from different directions.

The shadowy beings were drawn to Shin and Sophia, able to track them down with perfect accuracy. According to Micheal, even if they left the Dark Canyon and fled a thousand miles away, the Shadow Seekers would still hunt after them, following at a methodical pace.

You either killed them or they killed you. So long as you lived on this planet, they would never stop.

The duo managed to defeat their respective Shadow Seekers with relative ease the first time around. The Shadow Seekers were strong, but the Abilities, Artifacts, and individual skill that Shin and Sophia possessed gave them the upper hand.

Once a Shadow Seeker died, it would no longer hunt its target.

However… if that target remained within the Dark Canyon…

6 hours later, that Shadow Seeker would reform and begin its hunt anew.

Over the past 5 days, Shin and Sophia had spent a good portion of their time hunting down Shadow Seekers, over and over. The dark beings grew a little stronger each time they died, transforming from easy targets into, by now, considerably dangerous foes that had to be handled carefully.

It was a waste of time, in most regards. Shadow Seekers didn’t drop Points and this canyon was far from a good place to meditate. The time each Shadow Seeker took to respawn made them less-than-ideal training partners.

The only thing the duo had appeared to accomplish was to make their Shadow Seekers significantly stronger.

“Shin, do you need to rest? If not, we'll go immediately.” Sophia’s voice took on a commanding edge as she jumped up. The air fluttered around her as she activated her Wind Sweeper Ability, floating up until she landed on a large, five-meters tall stone boulder.

“Yeah, I’m ready to leave pronto. Let’s get the heck outta’ here.” Shin gave her a thumbs up. He pulled back from the edge of his stone pillar, wiping a bit of dust off his legs.

“Perfect.” Sophia’s eyes glinted as she turned her gaze to the west, in the direction of the Soul King’s Inheritance.

They may have wasted 5 days in the Dark Canyon, and 2 more days traveling to reach here, but it was fine in the end.

The Soul King’s Inheritance was known for its legendary treasures and mystical rewards, but the real reason Sophia and Shin were headed there, and why Micheal had them spend so much time preparing, was completely different.

Shin and Sophia had great potential, but they needed time to grow. They wouldn’t be able to keep up with Micheal otherwise.

None of the rewards they could possibly earn from this Inheritance could fix that problem.

However…

Rewards weren’t the only things that existed in an Inheritance.

Inheritances were, in some ways, a lot like games in amusement parks.

If you wanted to earn a prize from them, you first needed to complete a challenge.

The rewards earned might not be able to help the duo… but what about the challenges themselves?

The Soul King was the strongest Dark Wraith to ever exist, but not because he was skilled in battle or a legendary warrior.

He was a genius, not at battle, but in research. He studied things like Concepts, the Divine Language, and Artifacts, becoming a legendary figure in the era of Torens and Blue Drakes. Even Yvvtal the Destroyer drew from his work.

Far and wide, his name was known.

Tallanoran, the Soul King.

Master of Time.

.

Chapter 4



“Prepare to duel!”

“Condense your Weapon Energy, don’t spread it out!”

“Activate your Bane Flame Blades on my command!”

A series of gruff, wizened voices echoed across a sunlit grass field, demanding immediate action.

Hundreds of men and women stood in that same field, dressed in white leather armor that was emblazoned with the main symbol of the Purgatory Church: a large circle and three small circles that were lined up horizontally inside the large circle. These warriors were split up into several groups, each focused on various things.

Some of the groups held mock battles, while others went over ways to utilize certain Artifacts or Abilities. All of them were filled with determined warriors that were training without holding back, doing their best to improve.

The Nirvana Saint clasped his hands together as he studied all of this, his golden eyes giving away nothing.

The man stood at one end of the training field, at the edge of a rather thin forest, watching from the shade of a large oak tree. He was dressed in a set of humble white robes. He held no weapon in his hands or sheathed at his hip, but instead carried a file of papers tucked under his arm.

“Bevlin, how are the men doing?” The Nirvana Saint’s warm voice sang out as he turned around.

Directly behind the nameless leader of the Purgatory Church was a trio of men dressed in full metal armor. These warriors had the symbol of the Purgatory Church enshrined on their chestplates, making their allegiance very clear.

Each warrior was tall and strong, bearing sturdy physiques that were noticeable even behind all that metal. They stood at around the same height, a few inches above average for a human. Their helmets hid their facial features, causing them to appear almost like triplets.

One of the men in the trio, the one at the center of the group, immediately stepped forward after the Nirvana Saint spoke. This warrior emanated a tangible feeling of heat from his body, as if preparing to burst out into flames.

“Quite well, Your Holiness. The accelerated training plans have been implemented across all stations without issue.” Bevlin’s voice was deep, carrying a rich timbre full of confidence.

The Nirvana Saint nodded slightly as he studied the warrior.

Bevlin Petrov, the Sun Knight. He was one of the strongest warriors loyal to the Purgatory Church, and one of only six Knight Commanders within the Grey Knights.

“How about the reorganization process? Any problems there?” The Nirvana Saint asked another question.

“There were a few delays, but it’s moving along just fine now.” BevLionalswered in quick order.

The Nirvana Saint smiled.

“Good.” His reply was short, but contained a hint of genuine pleasure as he turned around, turning his focus back to the training field.

After the Nirvana Saint learned of the existence of the Beasts of Providence, he immediately began to implement countermeasures.

He was facing an unknown number of enemies that utilized unknown powers in an unknown world where he was forced to rely on incomplete information and unknown allies.

Given all of that, the first thing he had to do was obvious: Gather an army.

“Francis, Yun Chen.” The Nirvana Saint motioned at the two other men, elite Knight Commanders on par with Bevlin, adding,

“Return to your posts and maintain training. I want the Grey Knights battle-ready by next month. Go.” His voice brooked no argument.

“As you command, Your Holiness!”

“At once, Your Holiness!”

The two other Knight Commanders saluted the Nirvana Saint and immediately set off, transforming into silver blurs as they began to split away. A small entourage of armored subordinates joined up with each Knight Commander as they left, one group headed north while the other travelled south.

The Knight Commanders were the sub-leaders of the Grey Knights, the Purgatory Church’s hidden army, second only to the Nirvana Saint himself. Each one was stationed in control of six different areas, serving as a proxy for his orders.

The Nirvana Saint had completely rescinded the orders Archbishop Irin had left behind, calling the Six Battalions of the Grey Knights back into active training. The current training course had been designed by the Nirvana Saint, drawing on the experience of several military experts within the Church.

The Archbishop had weakened the Grey Knights, but not enough to ruin them. The Grey Knights had maintained their strenuous recruitment standards, all of their members were still elites in their own right. The Nirvana Saint had been gifted with an excellent foundation to build an army out of, something he intended to take full advantage of.

After reactivating the Six Battalions, the Nirvana Saint also weeded out the incompetent officers that the Archbishop had installed, reorganizing the military force to focus on discipline and competence.

This was a huge effort that was extremely difficult to hide. The Grey Knights focused on quality, not quantity, but there were still a bit more than 24,000 men and women serving within the hidden army. Even when split up, the movements of so many elites was bound to make waves.

No matter what the Nirvana Saint did, he was bound to be noticed. The secret organization that had controlled the Archbishop likely had spies placed within the Grey Knights, if nothing else. They might even be adding new spies to his army, infiltrating and controlling his men.

It was a harrowing realization. Trust was now an even rarer commodity.

The fact that he had been blind to the existence of this organization was horrifying. If he hadn’t learned of their existence and instead later been caught completely unaware… suffice to say, the consequences would not be pretty.

‘Speaking of trust…’ The Nirvana Saint’s golden eyes flickered as he glanced back at Knight Commander Bevlin.

“Commander, how go the preparations for the Great Feast?” The leader of the Church asked, smiling genteelly.

“Err- my Battalion hasn’t run into any issues helping the other branches of the Church prepare. I’ve been told supplies are almost fully stocked in most locations.” Bevlin’s reply came after a moment’s pause, the question catching the man slightly off-guard.

“Good, good. I’m glad to hear that!” The Nirvana Saint clapped his hands together, his eyes burning with endless enthusiasm.

Right after he clapped, in the distance, a white robed attendant slowly began to approach.

‘If I was the leader of a hidden organization and I wanted to control the Church, who would I want to dominate?’ The thought rose to the forefront of the Church leader’s mind.

A small glint appeared and then vanished from the Nirvana Saint’s gaze as he glanced at the attendant and then back at Knight Commander Bevlin.

“Just one last thing, Commander, before I let you go. I have a few last questions I’d like to ask you. Brother Gabriel, here, will join us to verify the truth of your answers.” The golden-eyed man smiled as he waved at the approaching attendant.

The Knight Commander shrugged and then nodded. The Nirvana Saint had phrased his words as if this was an optional request, but his tone made it clear that it was an irrefutable demand.

‘My first choice would’ve been the Archbishop. My second choice, however…’ The golden-eyed leader of the Church never stopped smiling as he studied the Knight Commander.

‘That would be the Knight Commanders…’ His smile grew a little harsh.

‘All of them.’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

♫…♫…♫

Beautiful music hummed in the air, singing a haunting, wordless melody that echoed in the hearts of all who heard it. It was an epic, a song full of bravery and hope, danger and fear, culminating in a hectic climax where everything came together.

Victory and death, defeat and life, a never-ending circle of stories.

♫

Micheal blearily recognized the tune as his mind wavered on the edge of awareness, his thoughts clouded and muddled.

‘Huh? What? Who?’ Try as he might, he struggled to form a coherent line of thought, let alone to search his memories and name the song.

He lay there for several moments, relegating himself to simply existing in the moment.

♫… ♫… ♫

It wasn’t an unpleasant experience, he found. In this state, he was vaguely aware of the many things he needed to do, but was unable to feel the urgency behind those worries.

Because of that, Micheal found himself able to truly relax, soaking in the raw music with a hint of pleasure.

Time slipped by.

♫

The song travelled down one familiar avenue after another, working towards its grand crescendo. It had its peaks and its troughs, the music dancing with a heart of its own.

As the song grew, so did Micheal’s awareness.

Gradually, various sensations returned to him. The first thing he regained was the ability to feel his body, swiftly followed by sensations of warmth, faint aches in his joints and muscles from lying still for too long, and a thick, heavy feeling that weighed him down.

‘Ah?’ Micheal’s mind gradually began to grow clear, his thoughts coming easier to him.

♫

‘The Life Festival… did I stop the attack? Is… is Myla Hannis still alive?’ The first coherent thought he could muster was not for himself, but for the Farians that he had tried to protect.

His memories of the battle with the Beasts of Providence rose up into his mind, as did the realization that there was someone controlling the minds of the secret organization’s warriors.

He’d stopped all the attacks he’d known about ahead of time… but given what he knew now… it was entirely conceivable the Beasts of Providence had had a backup plan that he’d missed.

A hint of worry rapidly began to spread throughout his consciousness, hand-in-hand with a feeling of guilt.

He’d been far too reliant on his knowledge of the future despite knowing that the history of the Second Layer was scattered and unclear.

He knew what he knew… but what he knew was not everything.

♫

The song that Micheal had found welcoming before began to grate on his ears now. It suddenly became discordant, rousing his consciousness.

Micheal’s mouth twitched, the muscles that controlled his lips contorting into a weak frown. His eyes scrunched up as he focused, doing his best to throw off the irritating tune.

His mind rapidly began to clear as his awareness rocketed upwards. Everything began to fly back towards Micheal, his memories rushing in without pause.

The final battle, the massive explosion he’d set off, the chain of Points notifications he’d obtained… everything came back to him.

Abruptly, the music vanished.

Micheal’s eyes flicked open, revealing a rather blurry room around him. He could make out a long brown bed that he was resting in, underneath a heavy brown blanket, as well as several windows letting in light on the walls.

What caught his attention most, however, were the two vague figures that were standing just to the right of his bed, one taller and one short.

“Oh? It was effective.” The larger of those two blurry figures spoke up in a deep, gruff voice that echoed out.

“Indeed. His Soul was already half-healed, my Spell only needed to do half the work. This human’s quite a resilient one.” The smaller of the two figures replied with a shrug.

Micheal responded by blinking furiously, clearing his vision as quickly as possible. At the same time, he split his focus in his head and activated his Life Orb Mastery Ability, creating a Life Orb that he could draw on if needed.

A few seconds later, the world around him came into focus.

As soon as it did, Micheal’s jaw dropped.

“Huh?” He muttered, so shocked that he couldn’t help himself.

Standing in front of him were two very unexpected guests.

The taller man was a Farian, a lean, muscular one with warm, golden skin and green eyes. His long blond hair fell across his shoulders, sliding off his square jaw to give him a rather majestic look. The simple brown robe he wore somehow complemented the feeling of awe he gave off, in an almost paradoxical way.

Micheal recognized him instantly.

He was Gregor Mantorel, the Lord Justiciar of the Farians.

The strongest Farian across the entire Second Layer, a legendary figure of great renown.

If the Six Lords of the Byrens were known as impossible monsters, the Lord Justiciar that could fight evenly with any one of those Lords was known as a freakish beast. Through his illogical strength, he singlehandedly prolonged the Great War Between Races time and time again, supporting his entire race on his back at times.

Gregor acted as the de facto leader of the Farians, though even his might wasn’t enough to force the Farian Tribes to smoothly cooperate. Still, he was a busy man, and not someone Micheal was prepared to see as soon as he woke up.

Seeing him now was surprising…

However, it was the second figure standing next to the Lord Justiciar that shocked Micheal to his core.

Like Gregor, this figure also wore a plain brown robe. He was of below average height, standing around 5 feet tall (1.5 meters). Instead of pale white or warm golden skin, his face was colored light blue. Apart from the odd color, his appearance was very human-like, with two grey eyes, normal ears, a small nose, and thin lips.

There were no Farians that looked like that… but the blue-skinned humanoid was the spitting image of a Rakkonian Wizard, one of the invading Races alongside the Farains, Humans, and the Orkals far to the west. The Rakkonians were known for their ability to cast mystical Spells and had landed in the territory of the Ground Demon Sect to the South.

Micheal’s breath caught in his throat as he stared at the two men, flabbergasted.

The leader of the Farians and a powerful Rakkonian Wizard, standing side by side at peace.

His mind began to race furiously as golden-skinned Farian looked down and began to speak.

“Good morning, young warrior. I’m glad to see you’ve finally woken up.” Gregor’s mouth widened into a smile that failed to reach his eyes,

“It’s time you and I had a talk.”

.

Chapter 5



Micheal forced himself to get over his shock, shoving his confusion to the side as he went into full observation mode. He extended his senses in every direction, his focus spreading outward.

The Lord Justiciar had briefly turned away from Micheal, taking the time to usher the Rakkonian Wizard out of the room.

Micheal seized hold of that opportunity to quickly check his Status. Just from the few moments he’d spent awake, he could already tell that his body had undergone enormous changes. Given his current circumstances, leisurely taking the time to sense each change one-by-one seemed like a bad idea.

‘Status.’ He instantly called up the glowing blue screen.

The Lord Justiciar turned around roughly 2 seconds later, just barely missing the wave of shock that appeared and then promptly vanished in Micheal’s eyes.

.

— - Status — -

Name: Micheal Care

Points: 621,885

Race: Human

Age: 18

Physique: Energized Physique - 2 Star -> Heartflame Physique - 3 Star Soul Quality: 3 Star

Strength - 268 -> 308

Endurance - 200 -> 227

Recovery - 133 -> 135

Soul - 38 -> 52

Abilities - (6/7)

Life Orb Master

Ki Cultivator (Earth Tier - Late -> Peak) Grandmaster Sword Mastery (1/5)

Impact Release

Ceaseless Mind

Temporal Bubble

.

’52! My Soul stat is 52!’ He stared at the screen, his eyes blank for a moment as he focused on his Soul.

Sharp, fiery, focused… if was like his Soul had evolved, the warm glow of Master Tier Sword Energy melding with it. His senses were stronger, his reflexes enhanced, his thoughts faster.

His Soul had fully accepted the Master Tier Sword Energy, underlining a transformation that could only mean one thing: He had become a Master.

“Congratulations on your breakthrough.” The gruff voice of the Farian Lord Justiciar brought Micheal back to reality as looked up.

The de facto leader of the Farians gave Micheal an amicable nod.

Micheal nodded back, his eyes narrowing slightly as he studied the Farian. He wasn’t sure if the man had noticed Micheal was now a Master or if he just realized Micheal’s Ki was half a step from Sky Tier.

‘…I already knew it, but he’s really a monster.’

After the transformation his body and Soul underwent upon reaching Master-level, there were certain things Micheal could see now that he couldn’t so easily before.

One of those things, in this case, were hints of the vast amount of power that the Lord Justiciar was hiding. Micheal felt like he was looking at an enormous explosion of energy that had been condensed down inside a single being.

If the two of them were to fight right now, with Micheal pulling out every trump card he had left and risking injuring his Soul, his chances of winning would still be less than 10%. Even escaping would be extremely difficult, assuming the Farian went all out from the start.

“Thank you.” Micheal returned politely.

Two of them gazed at each other in silence for a few moments, sizing each other up. A hint of appreciation appeared in the Farian’s eyes.

The Lord Justiciar smiled and began introducing himself.

“My name is Gregor Mantorel, the Lord Justiciar of the Farian Tribes.” He looked expectantly at Micheal.

“Micheal Care, a warrior of the Human Race. I have no title.” Micheal introduced himself honestly, giving his real name. If he wanted to get the Farians on humanity’s side, lying to them from the get-go would be unwise.

For some reason, the Lord Justiciar’s eyes widened almost imperceptibly when he heard Micheal’s name. His gaze returned to normal in an instant, but Micheal’s newly enhanced senses as a Master caught the change.

“I believe I owe you quite the debt of gratitude, young Swordmaster.” Gregor began, a glint in the Farian’s eye as he revealed that he had indeed noticed Micheal was a Master.

“If not for your actions, we would have suffered catastrophic losses.” The Farian stated the truth plainly, something Micheal appreciated.

If he had been a human commander, the Lord Justiciar might’ve tried to brush aside and diminish Micheal’s efforts or take credit for it himself. Not all humans were like that, but it wasn’t exactly a rare occurrence in Micheal’s first life.

“I was only doing what needed to be done.” Micheal replied without hesitation.

The Farians would prove a valuable ally if he could win them over to his side. They also couldn’t be infected by the Seeds of the Vile King, at least as far as Micheal was aware. The Vile King’s Seeds were only known to work on humans.

Over the next few minutes, the Lord Justiciar continued asking Micheal various questions about the battle that had taken place. Micheal, in turn, answered each question with clear, precise answers. He held back his urges to ask about the Rakkonian Wizard for now.

Their talk went on for some time. In the background, Micheal finished reviewing his condition. He also checked on his Life Orb count and found them to have been fully restocked. It seemed he had subconsciously managed to will himself to make new ones, a rather pleasant surprise to wake up to.

It also meant, given the 24 hour limit on Life Orb creation, that he had been unconscious for several days.

“How long have I been out?” Micheal asked when he found a break in their conversation.

“Hmm… since the time we picked you up, it’s been 14 days.” The Lord Justiciar replied.

“What?!” Micheal’s mouth fell open in shock.

‘2 weeks?!’

It was much worse than he had expected.

“Yes. You fell into some sort of transformative state after overdrawing your Soul.” The Lord Justiciar explained.

Micheal nodded silently, still not over his surprise.

His Physique transformed from a 2 Star Physique to a 3 Star Physique, his Soul grew astronomically, and he became Master Tier, all after an extremely intensive battle where he taxed himself severely.

Any one of those things would normally be dangerous, let alone all of them happening at the same time.

Still… a time loss of 2 weeks was terrible.

“We’ve heard much about you in that time, young warrior.” Gregor nodded.

Micheal frowned when he heard that.

“You’ve heard about me?” That didn’t make much sense to him, even if 2 weeks had passed. He shouldn’t be a well-known figure by this point, especially for the distant Farian race.

The Lord Justiciar nodded again.

“You’ve gained quite the reputation among your own kind, have you not?”

Micheal’s eyes crinkled up in confusion.

“Are you not aware?” Gregor paused, his head tilting slightly to the side.

“Aware of what?” Micheal hurriedly asked.

“All of our points of contact with your race have spread word of an enormous bounty for the ‘Great Traitor’ of humanity.” Gregor’s words resounded like thunder in Micheal’s ears.

“Micheal Care, a skilled sword user, the ‘Saintkiller.’”

Micheal’s frown deepened. He wasn’t certain how his full name had been leaked but it wasn’t too unexpected after what happened on the First Laye-

His thoughts cut off midway as his heart plummeted.

“Saintkiller?” He slowly repeated the last title as a sense of foreboding swept over him.

“Mm? Surprised? Well, it seems an apt name for who they say you killed… what was his name again… it was something weird…” The Lord Justiciar grumbled as he thought back.

“Ah, right. The new leader of the Purgatory Church.” Gregor nodded.

A historic genius that prevented the deaths of countless millions.

A prodigy that survived until the Sixth Layer.

An outstanding future hero of humanity.

“The Nirvana Saint is dead.”
