Chapter 6



‘Calm down.’ The first thing Micheal did was clamp down on his emotions.

‘You are in front of the Lord Justiciar of the Farian race. Steady, Micheal.’ The news he had received was shocking, but it was no excuse to show weakness. The Lord Justiciar was a Farian that admired the strong and Micheal intended on leaving the strongest first impression he could.

“I killed the Nirvana Saint? While I was resting here unconscious? Nonsense.” Micheal immediately latched on to the obvious hole in the story.

The Lord Justiciar shrugged.

“Perhaps it’s someone with the same name as you.”

Micheal inwardly frowned as his mind raced.

‘It makes no sense unless someone is intentionally targeting me. In the first place, I would never try to kill the Nirvana Saint. So… a propaganda effort, to isolate me?’ His eyes flashed.

‘The Vile King.’ It seemed Micheal had annoyed the mass murderer enough to get him to act, and on a massive scale at that. 2 weeks of time was more than enough for Constantine to set something like this up.

‘If this is the Vile King’s doing, that doesn’t necessarily mean the Nirvana Saint is dead.’ The closest thing the Vile King had to a ‘rival,’ in the original timeline, would have to be the Nirvana Saint.

The two foes shouldn’t have started clashing with each other for 1 and a half more years, but Micheal’s intervention appeared to have sped that timeline up.

Just because the Vile King claimed he was dead didn’t mean he actually was dead. The Nirvana Saint was incredibly adept at noticing patterns and unbelievably good at staying alive, especially in situations where survival seemed impossible, to the point where he earned the nickname ‘Holy Roach’ by some of his naysayers.

Despite telling himself that, Micheal couldn’t help but feel a little sick. If the Nirvana Saint died early on… it would force him to adjust almost all of his plans. Humanity’s survival would grow even more difficult.

“Regardless, you are a hero to our kind. After you finish recovering, the Tribe Leaders will convene a council to decide how to reward you.” The Lord Justiciar gently smiled as he continued.

"You have my sincere gratitude as well. If there’s ever anything I can do in return, just let me know.” The Lord Justiciar’s opinion of Micheal was extraordinarily high. He did, after all, stop what would have been the worst massacre in Farian history during their sacred Life Festival.

Before Micheal could give a reply, the air around him abruptly twisted with energy.

“Huh? Ah.” Micheal stuttered as he felt the Ki within his body begin to swarm and condense.

He was starting to breakthrough to the Sky Tier of Ki Cultivation.

‘Damn it.’ He frowned. After he woke up and realized he was just half a step away from Sky Tier, he had purposefully suppressed his Ki to avoid making a breakthrough. Clarifying his situation and leaving a good first impression on the Lord Justiciar had been his immediate priorities.

The shock of hearing about the Nirvana Saint being dead had thrown off his concentration, enough to allow the Ki that was raging to break through a foothold.

“Oh? The energy within you is… evolving?” Gregor’s keen senses missed nothing as he stared down at Micheal with interest.

“It feels quite similar to Bloodline Evolution. How interesting. This is the first time I’ve seen a human break through.” Farians grew stronger by evolving their Bloodlines in a similar way to Ki evolving from one Tier to another.

“My apologies for the surprise, Lord Justiciar. I didn’t think it would happen while we were still talking.” Micheal sighed as he began clearing his mind. There was no going back now; he would just have to make the best of the situation.

“Just call me Gregor, and it’s fine. The energy in you tried to evolve several times while you were unconscious. It’s why I called on an ally to help speed up your recovery process. I couldn’t just leave the hero of the hour injured without treatment.” The normally dour Lord Justiciar shared a mischievous grin as he added,

“I also wanted to witness a ‘Ki Breakthrough’ that I’ve heard so much about.”

Despite Micheal’s worries and the rather-pressing Sky Tier Heart Trial that was about to begin, he couldn’t help but to smile back.

“In that case… can I rely on you to guard me until I finish breaking through?” Micheal didn’t think he’d be in any danger here, regardless, but it never hurt to be certain. Losing concentration during a Heart Trial could have serious consequences.

The Lord Justiciar gave Micheal a look as if to say “Who do you think I am?”

“In that case… I’ll be in your care.” Micheal closed his eyes as he crossed his legs and assumed a meditative pose, putting his trust in the Lord Justiciar.

It took only a few short moments for his Ki to spread and then condense to the absolute maximum level it could maintain within his body, reaching his physical limit. At this point, even the slightest lapse in concentration could severely injure or even cripple him. While he could use a Life Orb to instantly recover from any injuries he sustained, there was no reason to waste one if he didn’t need to.

Immediately following this, Micheal felt the eerie sensation that was his Soul fluctuating as it resonated with the energy in his body. It felt like being embraced in a warm blanket while drinking ice cold water, growing hot and cold at the same time.

Light flashed in his eyes. His ears seemed to buzz. He could smell a harsh, arid scent.

Micheal blinked.

He found himself standing on a large, cracked stone plateau. Two suns glared down on the world overhead, lighting up a series of distant mountains and broken plateaus that surrounded him.

‘I’m back here.’ Micheal’s heart pounded as he looked around.

It was the Seventh Layer.

His Heart Trial vision was, for the first time in a decade, taking place at a new location.

“You humans are a lot like bugs, ya know? All that squirming and struggle for what? A meaningless death.” A jovial voice echoed in the air from behind Micheal.

Micheal’s mind grew eerily calm as he slowly turned around. The world around him seemed to slow down as he focused, staring at the speaker.

Behind Micheal was an Angel.

A muscular man with bronzed skin, dressed in a white robe. Long, beautiful white feathered wings rose out of his back, fluttering gracefully in the breeze. A glowing white Halo floated above the man’s head as he lounged atop a large boulder and looked down at Micheal with a friendly smile.

Murderous rage.

Unending hatred.

Extreme anger.

A torrent of terrifying emotions swept through Micheal in an instant as he recognized the speaker.

Navir.

A Titled Deity from the Sixth Layer, the Realm of Chaos.

The strongest Deity from the Angelic Tribe of Deities.

The Master of Nirvana.

“You.” Micheal spat out. He knew he was in a Heart Trial right now. He knew Navir was not actually in front of him. He knew this was all an illusion drawn from his memories and emotions that he needed to control.

Nevertheless, he could barely restrain himself as saw one of humanity’s worst enemies.

The Deity that destroyed the Purgatory Church and killed the Nirvana Saint. The Deity that annihilated the fractured Knights of the Round Table. The Deity that wiped out the Moorim Association and the Alliance of Saints.

Navir singlehandedly crippled Humanity’s Last Army before it could even begin preparing for the Seventh Layer.

“Why hold yourself back? Come, try and kill me- ah right, you can’t, even if you could.” Navir smiled benevolently as he snapped his fingers.

12 black and white orbs appeared, each one enshrouded in black and white flames, floating in the air around Navir.

Micheal inhaled sharply when he saw them.

They were what made Navir truly seem invincible.

Nirvana Orbs.

Micheal’s Life Orbs could bring him back to life after he died.

Navir had a similar ability. He created his own ‘Nirvana Orbs.’ Just like a Life Orb, a Nirvana Orb would shatter upon its user’s death.

Instead of simply reviving the user, however… Nirvana Orbs rewound time by 12 hours.

Each Nirvana Orb took 12 days to create, unlike the 24 hour limit on a Life Orb. Navir could control up to 12 Nirvana Orbs at once.

At any point, he could jump back 12 hours, 24 hours, 3 days, etc, as long as he had enough Nirvana Orbs. Killing Navir would merely send him back to the past.

That meant the only way to truly kill Navir was to kill him 13 times in a row, over a period of 6 to 12 days, all in which Navir had advance knowledge on how he was going to be attacked and the general future for at least the next 12 hours before each fight. This was also assuming that he didn’t just kill himself several times to jump back days prior.

Micheal took a deep breath. And then another. And another.

In the background, he could feel energy flutter in his Soul, rapidly building upwards as it grew and resonated with his body.

“Aww, don’t take it so seriously, little guy. Life is absurd. Don’t you know that already?” Navir fluttered his wings as he leaned forward to stare at Micheal.

“I only rewind time by a day here or two days there. You twisted Causality by more than ten years, you die a hundred times but still live all the same. If that doesn’t prove the meaningless of life, I don’t know what does.” The Deity laughed quietly as he lightly tapped on the floating white Halo above his head.

Micheal took yet another deep breath as he managed to calm down, a cool sense of rationality mixing his bloodlust as he gazed straight into Navir’s eyes.

“I will definitely kill you this time around.” Micheal’s words rumbled out as a vow.

“You won’t get even the slightest chance to survive.”

In the first timeline, humanity never killed Navir.

No one did.

The Deity left the Sixth Layer of his own volition after getting bored slaughtering hundreds of thousands of powerful warriors not only from humanity, but from a plethora of other races that were all climbing towards the Seventh Layer.

“Will you now?” The Angel tilted his head slightly to the side as he smiled benignly.

“The Great Traitor of humanity is going to unite an army to defeat me? Do you really think that will work?”

Micheal blinked. Even as he tried to ignore Navir’s words, he couldn’t help but acknowledge them.

The Vile King was not one to shy away from destroying his enemies. Micheal’s reputation was no doubt irrevocably shattered by this point. The fact that Micheal actually did kill the beloved Godfather of the First Layer meant there was a tangible foundation Constantine could draw on. After all, Micheal had no way of proving that Cameron had been infected with a Seed. From an outside viewpoint, he was simply a murderer.

“So what?” Micheal abruptly donned a rather crooked smile.

Navir stared at Micheal bemusedly, perfectly matching the attitude of the real Navir, a Deity that didn’t take even the strongest of humanity seriously.

“I don’t have to be the one leading the army.” Micheal’s eyes narrowed as he glared daggers at the Deity.

“I just have to point it in your direction.”

Navir took one look at Micheal’s face and burst into laughter.

“Ahahahahahaha. How utterly amusing! An army of bugs lead by- no, guided by, a broken failure of a man are going to kill me? ME?!” Tears streamed down the Angel’s face as he laughed in genuine amusement.

“Keep laughing, Navir. Go ahead. I won’t stop you.” Micheal’s cold smile never wavered as he regained perfect control of his emotions,

“I hope you die with a smile on your face.”

Micheal’s words were answered with another round of gentle laughter, one he promptly shut out as the fluctuations of energy in Micheal’s Soul started to rapidly increase.

A feeling of numbness swept over his body, his mind starting to grow fuzzy.

The Heart Trial was ending, unusually faster than his first Trial, perhaps because of his solid foundation and growth.

Light flashed around him one last time as he vanished, the vision dissipating. The waves of energy in his body shook mightily, and then folded together abruptly. A warm comfortable feeling settled into Micheal's body and soul as he blinked. Cool, blue light flooded his eyes.

Micheal successfully broke into the Sky Tier.

‘My Strength stat is 400! My Soul stat is 58!’ Micheal couldn’t help but to smile when he saw that. His Strength stat had grown enormously and finally reached one of the goals he had for it on the Second Layer, in addition to his Soul stat making fantastic progress.

400 points in Strength, the combined strength of 40 adult humans packed into one, was the baseline for the Lord Tier of Ki Cultivation. Micheal’s Directed Cultivation eschewing the growth of Recovery for Strength was showing its fruits.

‘400 Strength and a Soul stat of 58… if its me, that’s more than enough to kill most Supreme Warriors.’ Micheal’s eyes flashed with a hint of excitement.

The only exceptions to that would be, potentially, the Sect Masters of the Six Great Sects and definitely the Lord Justiciar of the Farians. The Orkals had no Supreme Warrior and were likely enslaved by this point, while the Rakkonians’ Wizardy was powerful but inherently slow, inhibiting them.

As for humans…

‘Of the Four Barons that are humanity’s strongest, Baron Rex and Baron Fortuna are the only ones that might stand a chance against me.’ Micheal cooly analyzed the situation.

Baron Rex was a figure that grew rapidly in strength over time, while Baron Fortuna was a human that obtained a Legendary Artifact from the Soul King’s Inheritance. Either one of them could have reached a sufficient level of strength by now, especially after 2 more weeks had gone by. Fortuna shouldn’t have gotten his Legendary Artifact yet, but this timeline was so far shifted from the first, Micheal wasn’t willing to bet against it.

‘400 Strength won’t be enough. I need more.’ His eyes flashed coldly.

He could not be complacent, nor could he forget his true targets.

The Six Lords and the Beasts of Providence.

The most powerful beings on the Second Layer were the Six Lords that stood behind the Six Great Sects. All six of them stood at the absolute Peak Stage of the Lord Tier of Ki Cultivation in addition to being experienced Masters.

The Beasts of Providence had a hidden army of experts, and an unknown number of powerful warriors backing them, as well as the Beast King that Micheal knew almost nothing about.

Agents of the Six Lords were actively experimenting on humans, while the Beasts of Providence were the Vile King’s secret weapon.

If the Second Layer was to become a safe haven for humanity, neither group could be allowed to exist.

Abruptly, something interrupted Micheal’s train of thought.

A new sensation spread throughout his mind, a faint, odd ‘tugging’ sensation that pulled him in a direction off to his right.

Micheal’s eyes widened slightly but then quickly returned to normal after he recognized what it was.

It was what came to be known as one’s ‘Calling.’

After arriving on the Second Layer, humans encountered a ‘waiting period’ as their Souls fully integrated with the new world. For two weeks, even if they were killed, no one would get any Points for their death.

After the waiting period finished, gradually, within a few days or weeks, people began to feel their own respective ‘Calling.’ Something that ‘Called’ them to a specific spot on the Second Layer.

Once you reached that spot… you were able to leave the Second Layer and move on to the Third. Everyone was ‘Called’ to a different spot, some distant, some close by. The sensation was easy enough to ignore, leading to many people that stayed on the Second Layer and refused to go up, scared of what lay beyond.

“Oh? Are you already done?” A voice interrupted Micheal’s thoughts.

Micheal blinked as he looked to the side of his bed, where Gregor was calmly sitting. The Lord Justiciar was smiling at Micheal with a hint of surprise in his eyes.

“Yes. How long was I out?” Micheal asked back as he rubbed his eyes. He frowned immediately after as his hand shot up, the vast increase in his stats throwing off his senses.

“…less than 5 minutes. Are all human breakthroughs this fast?!” Gregor rumbled as he crossed his arms, shaking his head in bemusement. When Farians went through their own growth periods, where their Bloodlines evolved, it was a drawn-out process that usually lasted an hour or two.

“No, I’m a bit of a special case.” Micheal answered with a smile. He had already gone through multiple Heart Trials. Even if the content of the Trials changed, his willpower to overcome them was immense.

“How’s your condition? You seem more lively.” The Farian’s eyes never left Micheal’s body as he looked at him with interest.

Micheal stretched his arms out before cracking his neck and shrugging.

“Within expectations. At the least, there’s no point in staying in bed too much longer. I should be good to go by tomorrow.” Micheal’s eyes flicked towards one of the open-air windows in the room he was in. There was a curtain blocking out the outside, but he could still make out that it was evening, drawing towards nighttime. If he stayed the night, he could use that time to adjust to his stronger body.

“Perfect! The Tribe Leaders will be pleased. They’re already convening tomorrow to see the Rakkonian ambassador off. You can come then!” Gregor clapped Micheal on the shoulder and grinned broadly down at him.

“I know you’ve been through a lot, so I’ll leave you to rest for now. If you need anything, there are attendants stationed outside to help you. Before I go, though…” Gregor took a step back, his grin replaced with a serious look as he stared at Micheal.

He then began to bow, his broad shoulders falling level with his waist in a smooth, formal movement.

“From the bottom of my heart, as both the Lord Justiciar of the Farian Tribes and as a man, thank you. I will never forget what you have done for us.”

Micheal blinked, taken aback. Being thanked like this from a literal legend was something he had never experienced.

Gregor didn’t give Micheal time to reply as he waved him off with a smile and began leaving the room.

“Get some rest, my new friend. If you feel up for it before you leave, come find me for a spar!” The Lord Justiciar guffawed as he left Micheal’s room.

Micheal stared at the door in amusement, shaking his head slightly.

‘What an interesting Farian.’ An honorable one, too, a rare enough thing to see for someone in power among any race.

After a few moments, Micheal shook his head a second time as he began looking over his Status again. He might as well finish checking everything out before starting some light exercises. Lying in bed for 2 weeks wouldn’t cause him any real harm, but his muscles felt stiff.

‘Wait, I have more than 600,000 Points?! Ah, I also have a new Physique. The Heartflame Physique. Let me check that first.’ Micheal felt ecstatic. Apart from the 2 weeks he lost, everything else seemed to be going his way right now.

‘Heartflame, 3 Stars, neat, neat. A Physique that contains a hint of the essence of a…’ Micheal’s hands trembled as he stared at the floating blue screen, his mind filled with disbelief.

‘WHAT?!’ Micheal slowly read every line of the blue screen, three times over, before letting out a rare, full-bellied laugh.

“Now that is something I didn’t expect to get. A Physique connected to a creature out of legend, second only to Dragons…”

“Wow. How did I get something like this?” Micheal murmured as he looked over the details of his Physique. After a moment, he shut his eyes and focused on his body, seeking out the changes it had gone through.

His senses had grown to a truly extraordinarily level by this point, especially after becoming a Master. Outwardly, he was he able to perfectly grasp his surroundings to the extent that he could now differentiate between minute air currents from dozens of meters away. Inwardly, even the most minor changes in his body were unable to escape his notice.

‘I see, I see…’ He thought, his eyes opening in wonder as he raised his right arm and stared at it. He clenched his hand into a fist and then relaxed it over and over, examining it.

‘Empower the flesh it says… hmm…’ He pondered.

His previous Physique, the 2 Star Energized Physique, let him rapidly absorb energy from the atmosphere. He was only able to achieve that Physique through perfect absorption of one of the extremely rare Magic Gems he obtained from Yvvtal’s treasury.

Upgrading one’s Physique from 2 Star to 3 Star was an enormous deal. The fact that most humans never even managed to get a 1 Star Physique, let alone a 2 Star Physique, spoke a lot for the difficulty.

While little was known about the process of upgrading one’s Physique, there were some things that were known.

When one’s Physique changed, it could only change in a way that built off the previous Physique. In Micheal’s case, his new Heartflame Physique kept the ability to absorb latent energy in the air.

As for its other effects… Micheal wasn’t quite certain of all of them. It was a Physique he had never heard of. He would need to figure out what it did by himself or, failing that, through his newfound Farian allies.

‘For a 3 Star Physique, it doesn’t seem to have boosted my stats any more than my 2 Star Physique.’ After scanning his body, he was able to make this observation with confidence.

His physical stats changing was a byproduct of his increased Ki Cultivation and his transformation into a Master.

‘Empower… empower… empower…’ Micheal frowned for a few more moments.

“Ah!” His eyes opened up wide as he noticed something.

‘I can feel the breeze in the air and I can sense the temperature… but it’s… different!’ His eyes flashed as he realized he was on to something.

After a few seconds, Micheal reached over and tapped on his Mid-Tier Spatial Ring, the Artifact somehow managing to survive a battle that literally turned him to ash at one point. After a few seconds, he withdrew one of the random items he had picked up from the First Layer.

A small, metal burner he had used when making Dragon Building Liquid for the first time.

Micheal set the burner down on his bed and then lit it without any hesitation. The flames flashed up but stayed contained on the burner, not spreading to the rest of the bed.

Slowly, Micheal reached out with his right hand until he was holding it a few inches above the live, burning flame.

‘Empowering the flesh doesn’t refer to making my skin tougher or muscles stronger.’ Micheal thought as he slowly began lowering his hand, bringing it closer and closer to the lit flame.

‘It means it literally empowers my flesh, imbuing it with energy… and transforming it like the flesh of a Phoenix.’

Micheal cupped the flames with his bare hand, the fire dancing between his fingertips and across his flesh without burning him.

A wide smile appeared on Micheal’s face.

“It doesn’t hurt.” It felt slightly uncomfortable after a few seconds, but despite the flame literally encompassing his right hand, he didn’t have even the slightest trace of a burn.

“Perfect internal temperature control, greatly resistant external temperature protection.” He muttered as he looked at the fire, entranced.

The Phoenix was a bird that could swim in streams of molten lava without batting an eye. They were famously immune to anything related to fire or ice, one of the reasons they were able to compete with Dragons.

“Wonderful.” This was a blessing he was not at all expecting to achieve. Its value was enormous, especially so when he thought of the future.

The 7 Layers were inherently inhospitable to humanity in many, many places. With this Physique that he had now, as long as he gave it time to grow and continue empowering his flesh, he would be able to completely ignore things like freezing blizzards or blazing firestorms without any qualms.

‘It also greatly enhances resistance to curses, mental attacks, and spiritual attacks.’ He noted the last line of his new Physique with a nod.

Once more, these were characteristics the Phoenix was famous for possessing. It was impossible to tame a Phoenix’s mind, impossible to damage their Soul, and impossible to curse them. They weren’t known for being unkillable for no reason.

“What a fantastic gain.” He couldn’t help but repeat himself with a slight shake of his head.

His new Physique might be lacking when it came to making him physically stronger, at least when compared to other 3 Star Physiques, but the defensive upgrades it brought him were simply unbelievable.

‘I need to ask how they healed me when I was unconscious. Perhaps I can obtain some hint on how I got my new Physique and gain a better understanding of its potential.’ He made a mental note for later.

“As for now…” His eyes slid over to his Status screen, to the massive Points total that he now possessed, as he spoke out loud to himself.

“Let’s prepare for the future. If I play my cards right…” Micheal squinted as he did some quick math in his head.

“4 days.” He nodded.

‘In 4 days, I should be able to get the Essence of a Deity.’

He thought back to the special reward he’d obtained on the First Layer.

You have become a hero of ages, a Champion for your race. As a conqueror, you will destroy your enemies while reaping the benefits.

A large stone castle stood proud atop a grassy green hill. This castle was built out of pure alabaster stone, gleaming in the dying evening light as darkness overtook it. Torches dotted the windows and insides of the castle, trying and failing to warm up the atmosphere inside.

Hundreds of Byren Martial Artists stood guard atop the walls of this castle, large teams working in unison as they went on patrol around it, circled the outside of it, or maintained watch from the ramparts.

Deep within this magnificent edifice, a massive meeting hall stood at the center of the castle, in the place where a throne room would have been. This meeting hall was sparsely decorated, lit up by dozens of large torches that plastered the walls, interspersed with ancient tapestries.

At the center of the meeting hall was a long, rectangular table made out of some type of green metal. Four Byrens sat on luxurious, golden chairs around this table, each one giving off Auras that caused the air around them to visibly distort.

Two other chairs were also present, but currently empty.

“Tch. To think they refuse to show up, even now.” The Byren at the head of the table grunted out loud.

The speaker was a weathered veteran, bearing a large, white beard and a tan, lined face that looked slightly at odds with his bulky, muscular body. He was dressed in a simple white robe with a black, diagonal stitching line that stretched from his right shoulder to his left hip. Currently, he was glaring at the two empty chairs at the table with a disgruntled expression on his face.

“Don’t blame them, Thunderfist. The signs of plague have spread to all the Sects. They worry for their disciples.” A soft, female voice returned.

The speaker sat to his right, a female Byren dressed in a tight pink dress. Unlike the first speaker that was unarmed, this woman had a long, silver spear strapped to her back. Her relaxed smile was decidedly at odds with the topic she spoke of.

“It’s damnably bad timing, Rose.” A new voice added, a male Byren that sat to the first speaker’s left.

This Byren was dressed in a black shirt and black pants, with a black bandana covering the bottom half of his face. He had his legs kicked up atop the table while he leaned back in his chair, his skin even paler than the delicate looking female across from him. A long, thin blade shaped similar to a katana rested on his waist.

“The Sanctum holds the ancient history of our ancestors and opens in just a few days. Plague or not, our forces are in disarray. Their absence is unacceptable.” A quiet, wavering voice echoed in the air.

The last speaker sat opposite the first. He was a small, kindly looking old Byren, dressed in a simple robe made out of coarse brown cloth. A long, wooden staff rested on his knees, one he kneaded slightly with wrinkled hands in exasperation.

If any other Byren Martial Artist had been present, they would likely have fallen to the ground out of shock as seeing the present figures.

They couldn’t be blamed for that.

After all, these four warriors were supposed to be mortal enemies.

Who could have expected that the Six Lords of the Byren race, the six hallowed experts that had been bitterly fighting each other for decades, were all, or mostly all, participating in a secret meeting together as allies?

The First Lord, Thunderfist, of the Divine Might Sect, a Master of the Fist.

The Third Lord, Roselia, of the Ground Demon Sect, a Master of the Spear.

The Fourth Lord, Shadow, of the Silent Sword Sect, a Master of the Sword.

The Sixth Lord, Whitestaff, of the White Mountain Sect, a Master of the Staff.

“It’s said they’ve gotten the plague under some level of control. If they travel with due haste, they should make it in time for the Sanctum’s opening.” Shadow lazily added as he yawned stretching in his chair comfortably.

“Aren’t the Farians in your Sect’s territory immune, Shadow? What’s with that?” Roselia glanced over at the masked Byren Lord with a quizzical look.

“Don’t ask me. Those savages live in huts next to the Dragon Mountains of all things. What intel could we have picked up from them?” Shadow casually waved off her question as he added,

“What about those weird Wizards in your territory, Rose? Or, better yet, why not ask the humans? They can create Artifacts out of nothing. They could probably pull off a miracle or two.”

“No one touches any more humans until after the Sanctum opens.” Thunderfirst’s deep voice cut into the two’s bickering as he laid one hand down on the table with a resounding thud. The hand was covered in dozens of thick scars and made the entire metal table tremble just off its weight alone.

“Yes, Thunderfist is right. Don’t forget our real purpose.” Whitestaff’s wavering voice added on with agreement as he looked at Shadow and then at Roselia with two eyes blazing with passion.

“The pathway between dimensions has weakened. The era our ancestors predicted is now.” The old Byren’s voice shook with excitement as he went on,

“In four days time, we will take the first step to becoming Gods!”

.

Chapter 9



There were three ways to replace an Ability as far as Micheal knew.

The first way, and the easiest, was to possess the Morphic Body Type. It was an unlimited Ability that cost 268,300 Points in the Shop. Humans with that Type could remove almost any Ability they purchased at will with no cost. The main exception was that the Ability couldn’t remove itself, thus requiring one to permanently have a Type that was versatile but not very strong.

The second way, harder and more restrictive but still not impossible, was the ‘Synergy Method.’

If one had an Ability that they wanted to replace with another Ability, as long as the new Ability was similar to the old, it was possible to ‘Synergize’ the Abilities through the Shop, replacing the old one at no extra cost.

What made the second method difficult was that the new Ability had to not only significantly overlap with the old in function, but the user also had to fully believe that the new Ability was a straight ‘upgrade’. If these two functions weren’t met and you had no available Ability slots, the purchase would still go through in the Shop, but nothing would happen, resulting in a large loss of Points.

Requiring ‘belief’ was a very fuzzy boundary with rather vague parameters, making this method unreliable for most people. It was also one of the favorite topics of debate for human philosophers and researchers.

The third and final method was the most difficult to achieve: find an Artifact that could replace or remove Abilities. There were many Artifacts that could do this, but all of them were extremely rare or extremely expensive in the Shop.

‘Hmm… since I’ll be obtaining the Deity Title Attribute, my choice of Abilities will have to change.’ It was a thought that had lurked in the back of his mind ever since he arrived on the Second Layer.

‘Let’s see…’ Micheal waved his right hand.

‘Shop!’

Limited Abilities, like their namesake implied, were limited. The only way to get an Ability that was maxed out was to either find a way to obtain it naturally, without the Shop, or to wait until the next Wave happened. There wasn’t any guarantee, but as long as a human that bought a Limited Ability died, there was a chance their Limited Ability would reappear in the Shop at the start of the next Wave.

His eyes trailed over the infamous Void Ripper Type for a moment before landing on the Immemorial Vision Ability.

He tapped on the Ability, pulling up its description.

.

—-Immemorial Vision—-

The Immemorial Vision Ability greatly enhances the mind of the user. It greatly strengthens the user’s resistance to all illusions and mental attacks. The user will be able to activate an ‘Energy Vision’ state, allowing them to see traces of energy.

.

This Ability had been one of his original targets, an Ability that would Synergize and replace his Ceaseless Mind Ability. The description the Shop gave didn’t do the Immemorial Vision Ability justice. Not only did it have the same function of giving him perfect memory just like Ceaseless Mind, it also came with a boatload of useful resistances and its signature Energy Vision that made tracking foes and predicting attacks easier.

Now, however…

‘My new Physique already gives me enhanced resistance to mental attacks, to the degree that it says “greatly enhanced resistance.” Buying Immemorial Vision on top of that would be overkill.’

The other perks of Immemorial Vision weren’t enough in his eyes. There were few beings that relied on illusions in the first place, so enhanced resistance to them wasn’t particularly useful. Even without it, Micheal could use his senses to overcome them to a certain degree. With few exceptions, no illusion was perfect.

As for possessing an ‘Energy Vision’ state… he couldn’t deny its usefulness, but was it a necessity for him?

‘No. If I’m going to get the Deity Titles system, then I might as well pick an Ability that will go well with it.’

The Pages of Ones was renowned for being the Shop page that contained the most Single Limit Abilities. It also happened to contain the World Matrix Ability that Director Prime used to stop time.

Most of the Single Limit Abilities on this page were part of the ‘Ruler’ Series of Abilities, a set of rare powers that always returned to the Shop when their owner died. The Ruler series was renowned for being extremely strong in the later Layers, most notably on the Fourth Layer, where the strongest humans had a Soul stat that could take full advantage of the Type.

Of them, the only one that wasn’t a Single Limit Ability was the Poison Ruler Type. Micheal was vaguely aware that there was a lot of history and lore behind the Ruler Series and why the Poison Ruler Type was Limited to 11 instead of 1, but never really bothered looking into it. He knew the characteristics and powers of each Type, anything else was irrelevant.

Micheal set those thoughts aside for the moment, scanning the list until his gaze landed on an Ability in the bottom half of the page.

.

Eyes of the Deep - 580,200 (1/50)

.

‘Someone already bought this Ability this early on?’ He paused for a moment, surprised. This Ability’s price tag and lackluster description made it last in the Shop quite a while, in the original timeline. Micheal's upgraded Soul let him overcome the 500,000 Points Wall of the Second Layer, but that was something that should be extremely rare, meaning the buyer had to be on the Third Layer or higher.

Micheal tapped on the Ability, bringing up its information.

.

—-Eyes of the Deep—-

The Eyes of the Deep Ability Divinely blesses the mind and eyes of the user. It greatly enhances the user’s resistance to Negative Energy.

.

‘It really is way too vague.’ He shrugged. Sometimes the Shop clearly explained things, sometimes it didn’t. There was little rhyme or reason to it.

Micheal’s eyes narrowed as he looked at one word in particular in the Ability description.

‘Divinely.’

In the beginning, there were many mysteries behind the beings known as Deities. As the years went by, after the Tribes of Deities overwhelmingly transformed into Humanity’s number one enemy, the layers of mystique that hid them were gradually peeled back. The results from the entire human race coming together to research something was nothing to scoff at.

One thing Humanity learned was that anything in the Shop that had the word ‘Divinely’ or ‘Divine’ in its description related to, in some way, the Deities. The Eyes of the Deep’s description was rather vague, but it did include the word ‘Divinely’ in it. As a result, it was one of the Abilities that was heavily researched, and thus one that Micheal happened to possess detailed information about.

This Ability fundamentally enhanced the brain and eyes of the person possessing it. Similar to Micheal’s Ceaseless Mind Ability, the Eyes of the Deep Ability gave its user a perfect memory. It also made his body and soul highly resistant to anything related to ‘Negative Energy,’ which covered a wide multitude of things.

More importantly… it gave him something that not even 10% of Deities possessed.

Divine Eyes.

Blessed eyes that could see through the essence of most things, or, in simpler terms, eyes that let him analyze not only Artifacts but also people, garnering information that would otherwise lay hidden.

‘No need to hesitate. This is my best option. Let’s get it right now.’ He had put enough thought into his choice over the past few weeks. This Ability would be invaluable for his future.

With that in mind, Micheal selected the Ability and focused.

‘I am upgrading my Ceaseless Mind Ability. I am replacing it with the Eyes of the Deep. I am evolving one Ability to another.’ He repeated this thought in his head, over and over, his willpower cementing it as truth. He only had one shot at this. If he failed, while he wouldn’t waste any Points, he would be stuck with both overlapping Abilities at the same time, taking up two of his valuable Ability slots.

Micheal’s fingers hovered in the air for a few seconds as he collected himself, taking one last deep breath.

Then… his fingers plunged down.

He bought the Ability.

A warm, comfortable stream of energy enveloped Micheal, gleaming in the cool air as he attempted the first Ability Synergy of his second life.

The next morning…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“He just stayed inside without asking for anything?” Gregor frowned after hearing the report from the Shadow Guards he’d set around Micheal’s room. Ostensibly, he set the elite guards there to keep watch, but they were really there to protect the savior that had saved the lives of many innocent Farians. Danger could pop out of anywhere on the Second Layer.

‘Perhaps there are complications from his injuries.’ The Lord Justiciar had thought the human’s injuries would be fully recovered by now, but wounds to the Soul were a delicate thing, after all. There was no way to be certain.

“Hmm…” The powerful Farian traced his fingers across the hilt of an ornamental sword on his hip, an Artifact that had just recently been brought up from the Farian’s First Layer.

The warrior glanced off to his right, his eyes narrowing.

He was currently standing outside a large wooden building, the Farian Council Chamber. The building was shaped like a sizable dome, essentially built as one giant room intended to host the various Farian Tribe Leaders.

It was rare for all the Tribe Leaders to gather together peacefully. Gregor could already imagine the arguments coming from inside the building as the leaders of the various Farian Tribes debated on their future plans.

The Lord Justiciar sighed.

‘I’ll check on him personally before bringing him over.’ Gregor waved the guard away and began to walk in Micheal’s direction.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“Yes!” Micheal smiled, his hands trembling ever so slightly with excitement.

‘It worked!’ He couldn’t hold back a smile as he called up his Status screen.

.

— - Status — -

Name: Micheal Care

Points: 41,685

Race: Human

Age: 18

Physique: Heartflame Physique - 3 Star

Soul Quality: 3 Star

Strength - 402

Endurance - 261

Recovery - 136

Soul - 58 -> 61

Abilities - (6/7)

Life Orb Master

Ki Cultivator (Sky Tier - Early)

Grandmaster Sword Mastery (1/5)

Impact Release

Ceaseless Mind -> Eyes of the Deep

Temporal Bubble

.

He successfully Synergized Ceaseless Mind with Eyes of the Deep!

It had been a grueling process that took several hours of meditation and focus to accomplish. He had been forced to stay up through evening, night, and now onto late morning before he finished. If his focus and willpower had slipped even one time, the Synergy would’ve failed. There was a reason Synergizing Abilities wasn’t a popular method.

‘My Soul stat also went up by 3!’ It was an unexpected increase. Most people that had this Ability saw an increase of 1 or nothing in their Soul stat. Micheal attributed the difference to his 3 Star Soul Quality.

Micheal’s eyes flickered off to the side, glancing at the light drifting into his window. It was late in the morning, but he should still have a little time.

“Ah.” Before he could do anything, Micheal’s stomach abruptly began rumbling, bringing him back to his senses.

“Right. I should eat.” He shook his head with a grin. He had been so caught up with upgrading his Abilities and taking in his new stats, he had ignored his hunger.

He spent the next couple of minutes scarfing down a set of warm pancakes and syrup that he spawned from the food selection of the Shop. He washed them down with ice cold water.

The Farians likely would’ve provided him with food and water if he had asked, but Micheal opted to spawn his own in out of habit. He couldn’t be poisoned if he never gave anyone the opportunity to poison him. Death might not be a problem for him, but being forced unconscious and held in that state was one of the ways to circumvent his Life Orb regeneration.

‘Alright, enough of that. Let’s get down to business.’ Micheal thought as he placed the remnants of his meal, a metal fork, a plate, and a syrup bottle, in his Mid-Tier Spatial Ring.

Micheal held out his right hand and stared at it intensely. He focused his eyes on it, as if trying to zoom in on his own body.

‘They said activating it should be something like this…’ He had never possessed the Eyes of the Deep Ability before, and thus wasn’t entirely certain on how to activate it.

For a couple of seconds, nothing happened.

Then, gradually, Micheal felt a strange, new energy fluttering within him. It wasn’t an energy that possessed raw strength, like his Ki, nor was it an energy that could shred through anything, like his Sword Energy.

Instead, it was a soft, pure feeling energy, cool and relaxing. This energy gathered itself within his eyes, causing them to glow white, ever so faintly.

A split second later…

A stream of information drilled into Micheal’s mind as a blue screen popped up in front of him.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Heartflame Human

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: C (Growth Rate: Uncommon or higher)

END: D+ (Growth Rate: Uncommon or lower)

REG: F (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

SOUL: B (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

MANA: C- (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

Path Notes: A human that walks a cluttered Path. Traces of the Path of the Sword, the Path of Time, and the Path of Rebirth are present.

.

‘It really appeared, just like the Status screen!’ If there was a similarity between the Deities and Humanity, it would have to be the fact that some of the Deities could create a ‘Divine Scan’ of an object or being.

Like the name implied, it was a magical ability that scanned something and listed the results in a screen that was almost identical to the floating blue screens from humanity’s Shop or Status.

There were some differences. For example, the names of the stats were shortened and were judged differently, like the inclusion of a 'Mana' stat. It also didn’t point out his Soul Quality or set aside his Physique. Instead, it called him a ‘Heartflame Human.’

Apart from humans, it was extremely uncommon for one to change their Physique, so this part did make sense. In the vast majority of cases, the Physique of a being was a permanent aspect of one’s genetics.

‘It has the spot for Title and Traits.’ Micheal noted with a nod. Those two spots were empty, unsurprisingly. They could only be filled by a Deity, or someone who gained the ‘Title System’ Attribute of the Deities. Likewise, the Path Notes weren't yet something relevant to him at his level.

‘And… it has my current Growth Ratings.’ Micheal sighed as he looked at the letters listed behind his stat values.

“Tch.”

‘I brought my Soul Quality to 3 Stars, have a 3 Star Physique that’s strongly related to the Soul, and have multiple Soul-boosting Abilities…’ He glared at the screen.

‘Yet my Growth Rating for Soul is only ranked at 'Rare or higher'?’ He rubbed his forehead with a sigh. It was lower than he had hoped for.

Growth Ratings were exactly what they sounded like. A rating that measured one’s growth potential in one stat or another. Those ratings served to estimate where a being would meet their limit when it came to gaining power.

Humanity only began learning how to judge Growth Ratings several years from now, but that wasn’t a problem for Micheal.

From Common to Uncommon, Rare to Heroic, and Mythical to Legendary, the ratings had an expansive range that made accurate measurements. Each designation came with an 'or higher' or an 'or lower' to indicate how precise a measurement was.

For most beings, these ratings were immutable and predetermined. There were some legendary potions or mythical herbs that could enhance a stat’s Growth Rating, but things like that were extraordinarily difficult to acquire, even for Deities, and not always effective. A potion that could raise a rank from 'Uncommon or higher' to 'Rare or lower' might do nothing for someone with rank 'Rare or higher.'

Before taking any Abilities from the Shop, the Growth Ratings of more than 99% of humanity averaged 'Common or lower' in every stat except Soul, which occasionally was ranked at 'Common or higher.' Humans, in terms of Growth Rating, were the absolute worst. Without the Holy Shop Attribute that humanity gained, it was almost assured that the entire human race would’ve never made it past the First Layer.

Even with the Shop, raising one’s Growth Ratings to a high level was not an easy thing. The various Abilities one could purchase had a large impact, but the most important one was what Ability was chosen as one’s Type. Some Type Abilities modified a human’s Physique while others just granted special powers.

Micheal’s Life Orb Mastery Ability, while technically not a Type, still locked him out of Type Abilities and, thus, made him fall into the latter category. This meant he had to grow his Physique, and Growth Ratings, through other means.

In his first life, by the time he died, his Growth Ratings were all ranked between 'Rare or higher' and 'Heroic or Lower', after a decade of hard effort and maximized training. Those Ratings didn’t sound grand, but they were considered above average in Humanity’s Last Army, though nowhere near the very top.

'If only I had been given more time to train… if I had picked a more optimal growth route...'

He tossed those thoughts as he reviewed his stats.

‘So in the Eyes of the Deities, I have a Soul stat of B and a Mana stat of C-.’

The Divine Scan showed a being's 'Mana' stat, which indicated the amount of Mana, Ki, Divine Energy, or any type of 'energy' in general that a creature controlled.

The Soul stat, conversely, indicated ability to control energy, ability to comprehend Conceptual Powers, willpower, resistance to mental and Soul attacks, and a few other related things.

'Hmm... It's not half bad.' He thought as he looked at his Growth Ratings.

The only thing that seemed odd was his 'F' rated Regeneration stat despite a 'Rare or lower' Growth Rating, but that was mostly due to his Directed Cultivation focusing all of his physical growth on Strength and Endurance.

Compared to his first life, it was an extraordinary amount of progress.

Humanity’s Status screen listed stats by comparing them to a base human’s stats.

The Divine Scan used by the Deities to assess each other obviously wouldn’t use human numbers, and, in fact, didn't use any numbers at all. Even the terms used to assess Growth Ratings were merely an automatic translation by the Shop. The real ratings were foreign, the Shop just picked an equivalent rating system.

As such, the Divine Scan ranked all stats on a letter scale. Any being that reached SSS in a stat was considered an Absolute Being, a Transcendent. Beings with multiple 'F's were viewed as little different than garbage. From 'F-' to 'SSS,' the scale gave an accurate measurement of a being's current capabilities without any sort of bias.

‘Well, a Soul Growth Rating of 'Rare or higher' isn't bad. It would've been 'Common or higher' at best around this time in my first life. My progress is already fantastic.’ Micheal consoled himself with a shrug. He was under a lot of pressure, but that didn’t mean he should set impossible goals. He would take things one step at a time.

Micheal blinked, his focus abruptly shifting as he detected a powerful presence approaching. His newly strengthened senses as a Master let him recognize the Lord Justiciar from around 50 meters away, even through a wall.

‘There was never any record of a Divine Scan of the Lord Justiciar…’ Micheal’s thoughts were tinged with curiosity. The diversity of Farian Bloodlines meant a wide variety of Growth ratings among their kind. However, most of the powerful Farians were killed in the Great War, well before humanity had even learned about the existence of Growth Ratings.

If he wanted to find out how strong the Lord Justiciar was, ‘accidentally’ scanning him with his Ability when he walked in was a perfect cover. There wouldn’t be a better opportunity than now.

‘Just how strong are you..?’ Micheal’s eyes began to glow.

‘Let’s find out.’

.

“I’m fine.” He most certainly was not.

Micheal had timed his Eyes of the Deep to activate precisely when the Lord Justiciar walked in. The Farian had knocked on his door and announced himself before entering, but Micheal had opted to not respond. It was a simple matter to pretend to be caught up practicing his Abilities, Micheal had been confident he could pull it off with no worries.

And, he succeeded. However, rather unexpectedly, Micheal found himself caught completely off guard by the results of his Divine Scan.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Primordial Farian

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: B (Growth Rate: Mythical or higher) END: B- (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher) REG: D+ (Growth Rate: Uncommon or lower) SOUL: B- (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower) MANA: B- (Growth Rate: Rare or higher) Path Notes: A Primordial Farian that walks the Path of the Sword.

.

The results were unbelievable.

A 'Mythical or higher' Growth Rating in STR, 'Heroic or higher' in END, and a 'Heroic or lower' Growth Rating in Soul. A low Regeneration Growth Rating wasn’t ideal, but it didn’t detract much from the other overwhelming Ratings, and a 'Rare or higher' Growth Rating in Mana was acceptable.

Even among Deities, a 'Mythical or higher' Growth Rating was extraordinary, let alone among mortals.

The Lord Justiciar was known as the strongest Farian in history for good reason.

Micheal glanced over the stats one last time. A Strength stat of B compared to Micheal's STR of 'C' was an overwhelming difference. His Endurance was likewise monstrous, B- compared to Micheal's 'D+', as was his Mana stat, 'B-' to Micheal's 'C-.'

The only stat advantage he had over the Farian leader was his Soul stat. While Micheal’s current Growth Rating for Soul was only 'Rare or higher', the enormous effort Micheal had put into growing his Soul was holding true.

Micheal’s lips twitched. Gregor’s grin grew a little wider.

“…”

“…”

‘I’ve gotten careless. Well, whatever. He’s an ally I’ll need anyway.’

“…I suppose I can tell you. You’ll hear it, anyway, in a bit.” Micheal murmured as he looked around, making certain they were out of earshot of anyone else.

This part of the encampment was particularly busy, with hundreds of Farians moving from building to building, some flying overhead while others walked to and fro. It was a bustling, warm environment that was at odds with the Slums of humanity. The Farian Tribes might not be perfectly unified, but they clearly took better care of their own than humanity.

Despite the crowd, the Farians willingly parted ways for the Lord Justiciar, giving him a wide berth out of respect. Several of them bowed their heads at Micheal, sharing welcoming smiles. The looks they gave him were so friendly that it made him uneasy. He wasn’t used to an atmosphere like this.

“It has to do with the true nature of the Byrens. More specifically… the true nature of the Six Lords of the Byren Sects…” Micheal began.

Gregor drew a step closer, interest sparking in his eyes.

“Go on.”

Micheal smiled with a grin that held no warmth as he casually spilled the biggest and most well-kept secret on the Second Layer.

“The vaunted rulers of the Second Layer, the pride of the Byren Race, the esteemed Six Lords…” His eyes flashed.

“They aren’t actually Byrens.”

The Lord Justiciar’s eyes widened in shock.

“What? If not Byrens, then what are they?!” Gregor asked in disbelief, his body tensing up. He looked like he wanted to run off right now and order an investigation.

“Have you heard of the Old Races that used to rule this world?” Micheal responded with a question of his own.

Gregor paused for half a second before nodding.

“Yes, just a bit, though. Torens, Blue Drakes, and Dark Wraiths. They’re all extinct or gone from this realm, and have been for hundreds of years.”

Micheal shook his head.

“Not all of them.” His eyes grew colder as he continued,

“The Old Races were known for constantly being in turmoil with one another. The Torens, in particular, clashed with the Blue Drakes and the Dark Wraiths in territorial disputes. The balance between the three races was solid for many, many years… However…” He went on,

“All of that ended when the Torens transformed into a race of Deities.” Micheal spat the word ‘deity’ out like it was a curse.

“With their newfound powers, the first thing the Torens did was massacre the other dominant races.”

In Micheal’s first life, human archaeologists and historians had teamed up to uncover the true history of the Second Layer. They never found out exactly what happened, but the hints they did discover were enough to piece together a full picture with a bit of guesswork.

“The Blue Drakes were slaughtered down to the last child.” In the end, they were only an intelligent Draconic sub-species, insanely powerful but not nigh-invincible. If they had been real Dragons, they might’ve been able to resist. There was still the mystery of how every descendant, from hidden, hibernating drakes to secret eggs, was destroyed, but the Torens likely had something to do with it.

“When the Dark Wraiths realized what was happening, it was already too late. Their species was originally small in number and easily brought to the verge of extinction.” The sheer raw power of any Tribe of Deities meant if one didn’t prepare beforehand, it was almost impossible to resist them.

“Most of the Dark Wraiths stood together and fought to the end.” Despite their ominous name, they were a brave and powerful race.

“However… a few of them didn’t.” Micheal’s face grew even icier, if that was possible.

“Six cowards chose to betray their comrades, giving away their location and using their own kind as a distraction to escape.” It was a classic story of betrayal that irritated Micheal. He couldn’t blame them for fleeing, the Deities were monsters that they stood no chance against, but to betray one’s allies was unforgivable.

“To avoid being tracked down, they abandoned their ghostly Spiritual Form and chose to take over the bodies of one of the races serving the Torens.”

The Lord Justiciar’s eyes widened in realization as he abruptly realized where Micheal’s story was leading.

“So you mean to say…” Gregor began.

“Yes.” Micheal cut him off with a nod.

“The Six Lords of the Byren Race are actually Dark Wraiths.”

.

Chapter 12



--

It didn't take much longer for Micheal to arrive at the Farian Council Chamber.

Outside it were several groups of Farian warriors, representatives of the various Tribe Leaders that were inside talking. Micheal glanced at the symbols on their clothes, noting that 12 of the 13 Tribes were present. The only one missing was the Kowalsi Tribe.

“Lord Justiciar!”

“L-Lord Justiciar!”

“Lord Justiciar, sir!”

A flurry of greetings rang out as Gregor led Micheal to the door. Micheal’s eyes widened slightly as he saw the literal wave of recognition and worship the Lord Justiciar was given.

‘Wow, the people really do adore him.’ It wasn’t a lie to call him the most renowned Farian. Powerful but friendly, strong but caring — he was a natural leader.

“They’re probably already going at it inside.” Gregor shook his head with a sigh, though he still managed to smile and wave at everyone greeting him.

Two Farians stood guard at the double doors that led into the dome-shaped building. The duo smoothly opened the doors as soon as Micheal and Gregor reached it, unleashing a wave of loud voices.

“…but that crosses the distribution ratio for the Reemer Tribe! We can’t accept…”

“…you even hear yourself?! Seriously?! Why, think of what…”

“…we please move on to the debate about the Rakkonian alliance proposal? We need to discuss the…”

“…”

‘Their soundproofing is excellent.’ Micheal’s first thought was an observation. He was a Master and yet couldn’t hear any of their voices until the door was opened. The building looked like a simple wooden dome on the outside, but clearly had significantly more thought put into its planning.

The doors shut behind Micheal as he walked into the large room. All the voices came to a pause as a flurry of eyes landed on both him and Gregor. Micheal returned their gaze with one of his own as he studied the occupants.

Sitting around a large wooden table were a mix of 13 Farians. Micheal could tell at a glance that most of them were strong, on the level of a First Rate Warrior. He saw several faces he recognized from the Great War, powerful Farian Tribe Leaders that were the bane of humanity.

In particular, his gaze landed on two specific Farians.

One was the Wise Lady, Myla Hannis. She was dressed in a simple purple gown that covered her from head to ankle, giving her a composed feel. Despite not being a Tribe Leader, he wasn’t particularly surprised to see her here. The title of Wise Lady didn’t only relate to research.

Myla smiled warmly when she saw him. He smiled back.

‘I’ll talk to her after the meeting.’ He needed to acquire Myla’s Beasts of Providence-tracking method, and what better way to get it than from the inventor herself?

The other Farian he kept an eye on was the closest thing the Lord Justiciar had to a ‘rival’ in terms of leadership.

A slim, handsome Farian with brilliant gold hair and bright yellow eyes. The man was dressed in a trim white shirt and flowing black pants, with a large, green longbow strapped to his back.

The Reginto Tribe’s Leader, Andron Galewing. He was known for being politically savvy and, after the Great War began, a ruthless archer that led the Aerial Division of the Farian Combined Army. He was killed by Baron Sansa in the original timeline, a year and a half into the war.

Every notable Farian figure was present except for the three hidden Shadow Captains and the Kowalsi Tribe Leader.

“Greetings, Lord Justiciar.” Andron was the first to speak. The other Tribe Leaders followed suit, some reluctant and begrudging while others glad and welcome.

Gregor nodded at them all and returned his own greetings before gesturing at Micheal next to him.

“I’m sure you’ve all heard about the Savior that did so much for us. Please allow me to introduce him to you all.” The Lord Justiciar cut right to the chase, before the Tribe Leaders could resume arguing.

The eyes of the Tribe Leaders felt like lasers piercing into his body as they all focused on him. Micheal didn’t flinch as he shrugged those gazes off and gave a slight, respectful bow, the proper form of formal Farian etiquette for a meeting like this.

“Good morning, Leaders of the Council. My name is Micheal, thank you for having me here.”

His greeting was met with widened eyes and a few surprised, but appreciative, nods. The Farians weren’t a very formal race, but that didn’t mean they welcome breaches of their etiquette. His actions were a minor thing, but led to a better first impression.

Andorn took the lead as he smiled at Micheal.

“On behalf of my fellow members of the Council, I’d like to extend our warmest regards to you, Micheal. What you have done for us is something we will never forget.” The other Tribe Leaders nodded in agreement.

‘Well then.’ Micheal thought,

‘It’s time to spoil everything.’ Micheal’s expression grew a little brighter.

People that made secret plans hated having those secret plans ruined.

Alongside that, if there was one thing people like that hated even more, it would have to be having those secret plans ruined and exposed for the world to see.

‘Let’s seize the initiative.’ Before the Council could thank him further or try to reward him, he began to speak again.

“I understand there is much the Council has to speak about today. Before anything, though, I’d like to share some urgent information.”

The Tribe Leaders all stared at him curiously. Andron, who had been about to speak, paused, caught off guard. The Reginto Tribe Leader blinked and then waved at Micheal to continue. While he wasn’t of higher rank than the other Tribe Leaders, it seemed that Andron served as the ‘voice’ of the Council when it came to leading debate.

“Thank you.” Micheal’s eyes gleamed as he immediately began to repeat what he had told Gregor on the way in.

“The Six Lords aren’t Byrens?”

“They’re Dark Wraiths? Aren’t those creatures supposed to be extinct?”

“What?”

“I’m not sure why this matters?”

He was met with a wall of confusion from the Tribe Leaders, which he expected.

‘Lead with the worst, finish with the best.’ It was a saying popularized by historians that described the propaganda spread by the Purgatory Church, straight from the toolbox of the Nirvana Saint.

Give the most shocking or hard-to-believe point at the start, then work backwards and explain everything as you went. If you finish your argument with solid points and evidence, it will resound in people’s minds and make your prior points feel more believable, even if you don’t have proper evidence.

“It matters because…” Micheal began, looking at each Tribe Leader pointedly,

“The humans that have been raiding your people are working under the orders of the Six Lords.” This was close enough to the truth to not matter. The Beasts of Providence shared some of the same goals as the Six Lords and were working in tandem.

A series of gasps and angry murmurs spread out among the Tribe Leaders. Myla and the Lord Justiciar remained silent as they studied Micheal, the two of them exchanging glances when no one else was looking.

“Explain.” Andron’s voice had lost all traces of warmth as he gazed at Micheal, his eyes serious and alert.

“First, there’s something you all need to know about Dark Wraiths. Normally, they’re ghostly, spiritual creatures that can materialize a tangible, physical body at will. However, the Six Lords are different.” Micheal reiterated on how they sealed themselves within the bodies of Byrens, causing them to fuse with those bodies and remain permanently physical.

“When the Dark Wraiths abandoned their Spiritual Form, they tore open enormous wounds in their Souls. These injuries are incurable and should have led to death within a dozen or so years.” Micheal held up a hand to stave off questions.

“Should have, I said. These 6 Dark Wraiths in question found a way around that…” He glanced around the Council, noting their attentive faces, as he went on,

“And that way is through death.” His words spawned another series of murmurs.

“After a being dies, these Dark Wraiths can absorb a small amount of innate energy that comes from a dead creature’s Soul.” It was something only materialized Dark Wraiths that had fused with a body could do.

“This energy can partially treat their injuries. It can’t entirely cure them, but it can abate their symptoms and keep them alive, and it's why they became the Six Lords.” Micheal took another glance around the Council Chamber. Several of the Tribe Leaders had dark looks on their faces as they began to comprehend what Micheal was saying.

“You all must have noticed how tense the atmosphere is here on the Second Layer. The Sects are constantly at odds with each other, breaking out into fights left and right.” Micheal’s words were sharp and gave no room for rebuttal.

“The Six Lords have taken complete control of the Byren Race and have been manipulating them into constant, repeated warfare for hundreds of years.” Micheal paused briefly, to increase the impact of his next line.

“And now, they are planning the biggest war this world has ever seen. A war that involves you, me, and everyone you know and love.” His voice echoed in a room that otherwise seemed frozen in silence.

Everything he said was true.

The advent of huge numbers of new beings on the Second Layer had given the Six Lords an opportunity they never dared to dream of.

Their injuries could be gradually staved off, but no matter how much energy they absorbed from dead Byrens, it was never enough. The Dark Wraiths had been in the midst of desperately scheming against each other when hundreds of thousands, and soon millions, of new beings dropped into their laps.

They had driven hundreds of thousands of Byrens to their deaths but still failed to cure themselves.

What if they killed millions of beings? Tens of millions?

They were creatures that had betrayed their own species just to slightly increase their odds of survival. There was no level they wouldn't stoop to, including mass genocide.

Regardless of the results, Micheal could not afford to allow the Great War to happen again. The losses humanity accrued were catastrophic and set them back years. If it happened again, it was as good as raising a white flag for their future.

“Even if what you say is true, how can we believ- hmm, wait…” Tribe Leader Andron cut himself off mid query as he stared at Micheal and pondered silently. Discussion broke out among the other Tribe Leaders as they talked back and forth about what Micheal said.

Micheal stared at Andron calmly, guessing what he was thinking.

‘I have no reason to lie to you all. No matter how surprising or unbelievable it may seem, I’m the Savior that risked his life to stop an enormous attack on your people.’

The Farians were firm believers in actions speaking louder than words, and Micheal had already proven himself to an immense degree.

“It goes beyond just the Six Lords.” Micheal broke into the discussion as he continued speaking.

“There is another enemy that we can’t ignore. The mastermind who helped direct the humans that raided your people.” A cold smile appeared on Micheal’s face.

‘Attack where your opponent can’t defend.’ It was another mantra pulled from the toolbox of the Nirvana Saint.

The Vile King had ruined Micheal’s reputation among humans to an almost irreparable degree. It was to the point where he appeared to be driven into a corner, hunted and hated by everybody.

However…

‘Who said I had to rely only on humans?’

“There’s one other enemy we have to be aware of. A vile man by the name of Constantine Lancaster…”

.
