Chapter 17



“A Seer… I see. So that’s how you came to save these old bones of mine.” Myla Hannis muttered as she stared at Micheal, her eyes lighting up with a fiery gleam.

The duo were standing alone in an immaculate wooden hut. If not for the crude materials, Micheal might have mistake the room as one in a highly rated hotel on Earth. There was a finely carved wooden table, plush chairs, Farian artwork on the walls and perfectly crafted glass windows. The room was even nicer than the Farian Council Chamber he had visited just a few hours prior.

‘What an utterly selfless man.’

The elderly Farian studied the human that sat across the table next to her, a human that had moved her hardened heart.

She had always told Gregor to believe in the best of people, whether those people were Farians, humans, or some other species. But on the inside, after witnessing betrayal after betrayal, even the Wise Lady herself had grown weary.

She said those words to Gregor more out of obligation than true belief.

The Lord Justiciar of this generation was an unprecedented warrior. It would not be amiss to call him the strongest Farian throughout the entire history of the Tribes.

Gregor’s personality was that of a benevolent hero. However… if that personality ever should shift to something more negative or tyrannical…

The mere thought was enough to make her shudder.

The Lord Justiciar was a walking weapon of mass destruction.

When he went on a rampage, no one could stop him.

She thought of him as one of her greatest friends and allies, but Myla was also realistic. It was, after all, her duty as the Wise Lady to plan for the future of the Farians.

She was no idealist.

However…

Standing before her right now appeared to be the very type of idealist she thought no longer existed in their world.

‘We owe him nothing, and yet, he has risked everything to save us. To save me. He did the impossible with ease.’

‘How ridiculously skilled is he..?’

Myla was unable to hold back a small smile as she looked at Micheal.

‘He reminds me of Gregor.’

‘…’

‘So this is what it feels like to be saved by a hero…’

Myla kept her thoughts to herself as she listened to the human’s reply.

“The knowledge I have of the future is frayed and incomplete, but it was enough to lead me here.” Micheal explained as he glanced at Myla.

“And… it was also enough to let me know how to fight back against the enemies that are attacking you.”

Several hours had passed since the attack by the Monster Class Morenkai. The Lord Justiciar had split away from Micheal to rebuke the security forces that were supposed to be guarding the Farian encampment.

In that time, Micheal had patiently meditated for several hours, calming his mind, body, and Soul. There was no use worrying over things he did not understand and could not control, like the unprecedented appearance of the Morenkai on the Second Layer. Instead, he opted to take a brief, relaxing break. His life was hectic enough as it was, the brief respite was one well earned.

A few hours into his meditation, the Farian Council ended up taking a recess. No decisions were made, but during their break, to Micheal’s delight, Myla Hannis reached out and asked to speak with him.

He immediately took her up on her offer, ending up where he was now.

Micheal went on to explain to Myla everything he knew about the Vile King, the Beast King, the mind manipulation powers he believed each had, and how that related to the tracking method Myla had developed.

He conveyed the information in a succinct manner, giving a speech he had rehearsed countless times in preparation of this very moment.

As a result, it took less than 5 minutes to convey everything he needed to share.

The Wise Lady was silent for a few moments as she took what Micheal said in, a small frown appearing on her face. The soft, warm look that had tinged her face was nowhere to be seen now as her eyes grew sharp and focused.

“The Beasts of Providence…” She muttered the name of the enemy group, her voice dark. The number of Farian lives that had been lost to them was not a small number.

Several more seconds passed as Myla narrowed her eyes, her brow creased as she concentrated intensely. Her gaze drifted off into the distance, looking past Micheal.

Finally, the Wise Lady turned her focus back on him.

“I have a question for you, if you wouldn’t mind answering.”

Micheal tilted his head to the side slightly before nodding his assent.

Myla pursed her lips, hesitating for the briefest moment, before letting out a sigh.

“Young hero, you’ve already done so much for us and I dare not ask anything more of you… but I don’t think you’re done with us.” Myla phrased her sentence more as a statement than a question as she went on,

“So…” Myla hesitated for the second time before asking,

“What are you planning on doing next?”

Micheal began to smile.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“Leaving already, eh? I can’t say I’m surprised.” Gregor’s deep voice resounded in the Farian Council Chamber as he stood face to face with Micheal.

The Lord Justiciar had a faintly annoyed look on his face, though not because of Micheal.

Another hour had passed since Micheal’s talk with Myla. In that time, the Farian Council had reconvened briefly, coming to a decision.

The Tribe Leaders would begin consolidating their forces in the aftermath of the Life Festival to prepare for a large-scale offensive. It sounded good on paper, but, because the Farian Leaders couldn’t agree on a more specific plan of action, the Council would have to meet again in a week’s time before anything else got done.

The Lord Justiciar had his work cut out for him if he wanted to get the Tribe Leaders to move as one. Micheal didn’t envy him one bit in that regard. The Tribe Leaders notoriously did not get along with each other, even during the midst of the first timeline’s Great War.

“Time waits for no man, especially not a Seer.” Micheal returned with a shrug.

Gregor eyed him for a moment, his face expressionless.

“Time might not wait, but the world isn’t going to end if you take a break.” The Lord Justiciar’s eyes held a hint of concern.

Micheal returned his look with a self-deprecating smile.

‘If only that was the case.’

For all Micheal knew, even a single day wasted could mean the difference between saving humanity and not, in the end.

“I’m serious, Micheal. I don’t know if you see it, but I do. You’re pushing yourself hard, too hard.” Gregor shook his head,

“No one can do that forever.”

Micheal shrugged.

“I don’t need to last forever. Just long enough.”

Gregor raised an eyebrow at that.

“And when is enough?”

Micheal's smile widened slightly, touched by the Lord Justiciar’s genuine concern.

He quoted the first half of a Farian proverb in reply.

“Death ends all duty…”

“…but duty’s end is not death.” Gregor grimaced as he finished the proverb, heaving a sigh.

“You’re surprisingly well informed on Farian culture.”

Micheal tapped his head twice and smirked.

“Perks of being a Seer.”

The Lord Justiciar chuckled despite himself.

“Alright, alright.” He waved at Micheal and shook his head, giving up on persuading him.

“Well, before you go, take this.”

The Lord Justiciar abruptly hurled a long, thin object at Micheal’s chest, pulling it out of seemingly nowhere.

“It’s a reward you’ve more than earned.”

Micheal’s hands snaked out and grabbed the package mid-air. Somewhat embarrassingly, he was forced to spawn a Time Bubble that slowed down time in order to react fast enough to catch it. Gregor’s eyes gleamed as he saw this, his curiosity at Micheal’s unusual powers clearly still going strong.

“A sword?” Micheal muttered as he ran his hand along a long, grey leather sheath. The leathery hide was carved with long, sinuous patterns that looped up and down it, stained a faint red.

He slowly pulled the blade out, unleashing a faint blue glow into the Council Chamber.

‘Is this..? It is.’ His eyes quivered for a moment as rubbed the glittering blue blade.

‘It’s a sword made out of Blood-Refined Mithril.’

It was a reward that he absolutely did not expect to get… a fantastic reward.

Throughout the entire population of Farians on the Second Layer, the number of Blood-Refined Mithril weapons that existed could be counted on a single hand.

It was a weapon crafted from a type of magical ore, enchanted with the life force of tens of thousands of Farians, smithed into existence by a grandmaster smith. Each weapon was ancient, forged in the days where tribal warfare was commonplace and sacrificing enemy Tribemembers was acceptable.

‘If it was listed in the Shop, this sword’s value would be tremendous. Easily over 300,000 Points, 400,000 Points, maybe more.’

Blood-Refined Mithril weapons were indescribably durable, had the ability to regenerate from any damage sustained, could perfectly convey any energy that was imbued into it, and had the ability to adjust their shape, scale, and even weight to match the preference of its owner.

‘Each Blood-Refined Mithril sword is considered an Ancestral Artifact of the upmost value.’

Micheal tore his loving gaze away from the sword and looked back up at Gregor, a far too warm smile appearing on his face.

Gregor shuddered.

“Don’t look at me like that, just take the damn sword and go. I don't want to hear your thanks.” The Lord Justiciar flared his hand out and made a brushing motion, as if to blow Micheal away.

“I have paperwork to do, even now, in this damned apocalypse.” Gregor sat down at the table of the Council Chamber, grumbling as he pulled out a large stack of parchment.

“The sword’s name is Lightshorn. Don’t lose it.”

Micheal nodded quietly as he looked down at the sword for a few more seconds, only the sound of paper rustling in the still air.

He then took a deep breath and turned around, his gaze growing fierce as he began to walk towards the exit.

Just before he left, the Lord Justiciar’s voice echoed one last time.

“Try not to die out there.”

Micheal looked back at Gregor and gave him a rather cheeky grin.

“No promises.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

A cool breeze ruffled over Micheal’s hair, carrying the refreshing scent of flowers, trees, and desolated, smoky earth.

Micheal glanced at the forest that spread out in front of him to the South of the Farian encampment, the aftermath of his explosive attack on the Beasts of Providence staining the ground not too far away.

It was time to go…

But this time…

Micheal looked behind him at the more than 200 Farian warriors garbed in grey leather armor, powerful members of the elite Shadow Guard, armed to the teeth.

Standing at the front of this group was a thick, muscular warrior with stark yellow hair and a grizzled yellow beard that had a few hints of grey, wearing a two meters long stone pillar on his back.

Right next to the older warrior was a younger female Farian with long brown hair that complemented her lean, tanned physique. Her face was dotted with freckles and her eyes glowed with a red fiery gleam.

“Shadow Captain Sprel.” Micheal looked at the veteran fighter,

“Disciple Apparent Serena.” He turned his gaze to the younger adult female, the direct, and only, disciple of the Wise Lady herself.

It was time to go…

But this time…

Micheal’s eyes crinkled in a smile.

This time…

He was bringing an army.

“Let’s go.”

.

Chapter 18



In the depths of the Dark Canyon, there existed a rather normal looking stone wall.

This wall was marked with cracks and creases, weathered and aged by the sands of time. From first glance, it didn’t seem any different than the many other stone boulders and cliffs around it. The Dark Canyon stretched for hundreds of miles, after all, with much of the same scenery repeated over and over.

Standing in front of this unremarkable wall was a young woman dressed in a simple brown dress and boots, resting the palm of her right hand on two sheathed shortswords attached to a belt around her waist.

“This is the spot.” Sophia muttered as she stared at the wall, her Fairy Eyes glowing with faint pink light.

The Limited Ability not only allowed her to befuddle her enemies with stunningly realistic illusions but also enhanced her vision dramatically, allowing her to see things others couldn’t.

“Really? I don’t see anything different.” Shin abruptly teleported into existence next to Sophia, squatting down on the ground and staring at the wall suspiciously.

“It just is, it’s hard to describe. It looks… weird. This should be the spot.” Sophia shrugged as she stared at the wall.

“You already killed your Shadow Seeker, now I just need to kill mine.” Sophia turned away from the nondescript wall and began to pan her eyes around, scanning the environment.

The mostly empty canyon was eerily silent, the afternoon light faded and dim due to the ever-present cloud cover above.

Behind Sophia, the ordinary stone wall seemed to shiver ever so faintly as Shin walked near it.

The Soul King’s Inheritance had laid here undiscovered in this location for thousands of years, and that was for good reason.

Not only was it located in one of the danger zones of the Second Layer, the Dark Canyon, but it also was incredibly difficult to spot.

In the first timeline, this ancient tomb was discovered by someone with the Pathfinder Type Ability, an Ability that used mystical energy to seek out lost treasures, hidden relics, and places that housed great secrets. If humanity never came to the Second Layer, it was quite conceivable that the tomb would never be discovered again.

It was an unusual Inheritance; most Inheritances were designed to be difficult to complete, not difficult to find at all. If anything, the Soul King’s Inheritance went against the norm…

Which was intentional, as it turned out.

The Soul King’s Inheritance wasn’t designed to be discovered by humans, Byrens, or any of the main races on the Second Layer in the first place.

It was a tomb meant to be found by the brethren of the Soul King: the nigh extinct Dark Wraiths.

“Well, alright. I’ll set up watch.” Shin waved at Sophia and then vanished, teleporting dozens of meters away to a high vantage point near the top of the canyon. He pulled out his sleek Soul Rifle and began to adjust its aim, panning up and down the canyon as he looked for enemies.

The teamwork between the duo had grown exponentially after working together the past several weeks. Shin had grown into the role of a scout and teleporting sharpshooter, while Sophia put every iota of her being into mastering close combat.

Sophia took a deep breath as she sat down on a nearby boulder, crossing her legs comfortably. From her waist, she pulled out two grey shortswords, each one an Artifact called a Dust Blade from the Shop. The swords cost 36,780 Points each, Sophia had managed to get both by hunting Morenkai on the First Layer, just before she and Shin went up to the Second.

The swords were sharp, with a smaller-than-average grip that fit perfectly into Sophia’s hands. Each weapon had the special property that, when charged with Ki, emitted trails of grey dust that floated in the air, obstructing the vision of her targets. The swords weren’t perfect, the dust trails also blocked her own view, but with her ability to manipulate wind thanks to her Wind Sweeper Ability, the downsides could be minimized.

Time passed by.

Minutes slipped away as Sophia sat and meditated, breathing in and out at a steady pace, focusing her senses outward. Her entire body relaxed and entered a state of calm readiness.

Finally, after roughly 10 minutes of waiting…

“Incoming from the East, Sofa!” Shin’s voice echoed out loud.

Immediately, Sophia’s head snapped to her right, staring towards the direction Shin pointed out.

Roughly 400 meters out, She could just make out a vague, shadowy figure moving towards her. The Shadow Seeker’s body came into focus as it rushed at her, a replica of Sophia herself.

Sophia stood up, spreading her two short swords out and to the side. Her Fairy Eyes flashed pink as she enhanced her vision. While her Fairy Eyes couldn’t trap the Shadow Seeker in an world of illusions, it did make time around her seem to slow down when she zeroed in on her opponent, proving to be more than helpful.

The air around Sophia began to fluctuate as she activated her Wind Sweeper Ability, manipulating the wind around her.

As the air began to whip behind her, she bent her knees and faced the charging shadowy copy of herself.

The Shadow Seeker, by this point, had blitzed towards Sophia at an incredible speed. After being hunted for 5 days in a row, this iteration of Shadow Seeker had grown to be extremely fast and strong.

In just a few split seconds, it sprinted more than 375 meters, its body transforming to a blur. Every step the creature took seemed to almost glide off the ground, leaving no trail or trace behind.

Sophia never lost track of the monster as she stared it down quietly, her body tensing up as it grew close.

‘It’s still just as unnerving as before.’ She thought in the moment before it reached her.

Shadow Seekers made little to no sound, unlike a normal monster. They didn’t pant or growl and their movements had almost no interaction with the surrounding environment… if it wasn’t for the murderous chase and attacks against their targets, it was almost like they didn’t exist at all.

The creature arrived and attacked.

When Micheal told Sophia about the Shadow Seekers, he had described them in a rather succinct way.

‘When you’re outside the Soul King’s Inheritance, think of them like super-strong Morenkai that come back stronger every 6 hours after you kill them. They can block attacks and move stealthily, but that’s the limit to their intelligence.’

In a similar vein to how the Morenkai fought, the Shadow Seeker lunged at Sophia with both hands, slamming one in from each side in a sort of murderous hug attempt. Despite its simple nature, the attack was not something Sophia would survive if it landed on her. Even a single glancing blow from this Shadow Seeker would be enough to break several bones in her body, while a full on attack would fatally injure her.

‘But it has to actually land that attack first.’ Sophia’s eyes flashed as she kicked her right foot off the ground, winds of over 100 mph rocketing her upward in one smooth, graceful motion.

She flipped over the Shadow Seeker, dodging its attack completely.

The Shadow Seeker noticed immediately and twisted its body as it began to turn, eerily silent as it lurched to a halt. The creature slid across the ground as it forcibly cancelled its momentum.

In the midst of her flip, while she was still upside-down and mid-air, Sophia pulled her right arm in, clutching the Dust Blade tight and covering it with the glow of Intermediate Tier Sword Energy, rippling power that showed the faintest hints of evolving into Advanced Sword Energy.

A split second later, just as the Shadow Seeker was beginning to turn, Sophia flung her right arm forward with all her might, sending the short sword hurtling through the air towards the Shadow Seeker and leaving a trail of floating dust.

Deft, guided winds sprung into existence and accelerated the blade, blasting it forth even faster.

And, in the same split second the Shadow Seeker took to turn around…

Sophia’s glittering sword slammed into its chest and pierced it down to the hilt, bringing the creature to a stuttering halt.

Sophia took advantage of that halt as, while still upside down and in mid-air, she formed a platform of solid air and kicked off that platform, spinning her body around to land on her feet right in front of the Shadow Seeker.

The Shadow Seeker tried to react, its inhuman durability letting it overcome the shock of getting stabbed through the chest. The trail of floating dust in front of its chest partially obscured its vision, forcing it to lash out wildly at Sophia.

Sophia crouched supernaturally fast by manipulating the wind to help her duck down, while simultaneously raising her other remaining Dust Sword up in a defensive block.

The Shadow Seekers right arm flew over her head, missing completely, while its left arm got deflected by Sophia’s raised sword, glancing off at an angle. The power behind the blow was enough to make Sophia’s left arm go numb, but unable to injure her.

There was a split moment in time where neither Sophia nor the Shadow Seeker were attacking each other. Sophia’s left arm had been knocked outward, her Dust Sword nearly flying from her grip at the force of the monster’s attack, while the Shadow Seekers arms hung loose and awkwardly out.

That moment ended as Sophia’s right hand snaked up and grabbed the Dust Sword that was pierced through the Shadow Seeker’s chest.

She latched onto the grey sword and then ripped it up vertically, instantly splitting the monster’s chest, neck, and head in half in a fraction of a second as she stood up.

The Shadow Seeker immediately died, black, shadowy essence spattering through the air in a wide arc from Sophia’s attack.

“Tch.” A stiff breeze rustled over Sophia, making sure none of the black substance landed on her as she cleaned off her sword and stepped away.

“Strength without skill is no strength at all.” Sophia muttered a quote she’d heard Micheal say as she looked at the remains of the creature, her eyes cold and calm as she sheathed her shortswords.

In that moment, if Micheal had been there, he would’ve been unable to hold back a smile.

Sophia Morgan, the infamous Demon Fairy of the first timeline, was officially back.

A genius who possessed an incredible ability to adapt, learn, and fight, a veritable monster in her own right, one of the strongest First Layer S Rankers.

“Woah, nice job. You’re getting kinda scary now, Sofa.” Shin’s voice sounded off right next to her as he popped in out of nowhere, teleporting beside her. Shin had his Soul Rifle aimed down, but still at the ready, in case the Shadow Seeker was somehow not dead.

“Let’s not fight each other, like, ever.”

Sophia rolled her eyes.

“It’s dead now, let’s not waste any more time.” She replied as she began walking over to the nondescript entrance to the Soul King’s Inheritance.

“Alright, alright. Fair enough. I was getting bored of killing these things over and over anyway.” Shin shrugged and walked up behind her, his cheerful demeanor dampening as his gaze grew a little more serious.

“I guess we finally get to see why Micheal had us do that.”

Sophia lifted her right hand up to the stone wall, storing her two Dust Blades in her Spatial Ring as she did so. She carefully rested her hand on the cracked stone and waited.

Only a couple of seconds after she touched the rock, warm, yellow light began to appear, emanating from all the nearby cracks in a 5 meter radius. From this light, strange symbols began to emerge, glowing yellow glyphs that surrounded both Sophia and Shin.

Sophia took it all in steadfastly while Shin gazed about in delight, waving his hand through the glyphs to see what happened. Nothing, as it turned out. Sophia shot him a glare in response.

And then…

Just like that, the duo vanished, the glowing symbols exploding with light and teleporting them away.

The light slowly faded away from the rocky wall. Soon, this area of the Dark Canyon returned to normal, looking just as boring and uninteresting as any other part.

…

Sophia and Shin had successfully entered the Soul King’s Inheritance.

.

Chapter 19



On the Second Layer, there were thousands and thousands of Inheritances, ancient legacies and burial grounds left behind by powerful warriors, Masters, and beings of great power. It was a unique tradition that could only be found on the Ancient World and not something present on any of the other Layers.

In the first timeline, various research groups that housed the best of humanity’s scientists believed that the First Layer was an artificial world created just to welcome humanity into the 7 Layers. They used a number of methods, from pseudo-carbon dating the dirt found on the dangerous ground level of the First Layer, to using mystical powers purchased in the Shop to further their research.

The Second Layer, the Ancient World, was not like that. It was a real, existing world that forcibly hosted the Second Layer, ignoring the will of its original inhabitants. The world had a rich history, a complex past, and an even more complicated present.

The fact that Inheritances existed and could grant great treasures or hold powerful legacies was not a secret to the Byrens.

In fact, almost all known Inheritances had already been ransacked. Byren Martial Artists would often leave their Sects to go on journeys through the Ancient World, expanding their mindset, gaining experience, and hunting for these rare treasure grounds.

New Inheritances were found relatively often… but most were relatively mediocre and quickly looted.

Rare exceptions existed in the form of extraordinary Inheritances that contained great treasures, but those Inheritances received an extreme level of attention and competition. Once an Inheritance of that level was accessed, the various scrying and searching methods developed over the years to find Inheritances would inevitably let others know of its existence.

The only extraordinary Inheritances that remained, in the current era, were either extremely difficult to find, like Yvvtal’s Inheritance, or extraordinarily difficult to complete, like the famous Draconic Twelve Tombs.

In the case of the Soul King’s Inheritance, it was both.

Tallanoran, the Soul King, was one of the fallen heroes that fought in a grand war between the Deified Torens, the Dark Wraiths, and the Blue Drakes, the three dominant species of the Ancient World in the past.

Very little was known about the long forgotten past of the Ancient World. Micheal, in the first timeline, had done quite a bit of research into this out of personal interest. When the modern Great War Between Races broke out on the Second Layer, many hidden truths were unveiled to the world, though much more was lost.

According to what Micheal learned from Yvvtal, some time, long ago, the Torens unlocked the secrets of the Divine Language and attained Divinity.

It was around this period, as the Torens Ascended and become a Tribe of Deities, that a massive, world war unfolded.

The Deified Torens went on a rampage with the singular goal of exterminating the Blue Drakes and the Dark Wraiths, their longtime rivals.

The Dark Wraiths were virtually annihilated while the Blue Drakes vanished, many believing them to have been slaughtered down to the last child, the remainder forced to flee to a different plane of existence.

The Soul King was a Dark Wraith that had personally fought against the attacking Deities. He was a Master of Time, able to wield Time Energy like a Swordmaster wielded Sword Energy.

He was the sole reason that the Dark Wraiths were not immediately wiped out when the Torens began their attack. If not for the fact that 6 Dark Wraiths betrayed the others and fled, exposing their allies' location to buy time for themselves to escape, Tallanoran might have resisted the Torens for even decades more.

A single warrior holding off against a Tribe of Deities, albeit, a newly born and comparatively weak Tribe of Deities, was an enormous achievement.

Sophia knew bits and pieces of this history thanks to Micheal, missing only the information that Yvvtal had shared.

She kept these thoughts to herself she teleported inside the Inheritance, immediately going on guard as the flashing light enveloped her.

In a split second, she found herself inside the Inheritance, standing alongside Shin on a large, circular platform.

Sophia blinked furiously as her eyes adjusted to the dim room, scanning the environment.

“This place feels kinda creepy.” Shin muttered as he looked around. After a few seconds, he silently pulled up the description of his teleporting Ability.

.

—- Phasing Warper Type —-

The Phasing Warper Ability is a Type Ability. Users may only have one Type. The Phasing Warper Ability grants the user the power to 'Phase' through reality, warping from one place to another at near instantaneous speeds. This Ability grants a moderate increase in the Soul stat and no other bonuses.

.

‘Micheal said this Inheritance is like a mini-distorted world of its own, with holes of wonky spacetime.’ Shin paraphrased Micheal’s description as he activated his Ability.

‘Will I be able to teleport here?’

Shin’s eyes gleamed ever so faintly.

Instantly, his vision was overlaid with a world of translucent lines of energy, like tiny ropes connecting one place to another. These small ropes appeared woven within the fabric of space itself, keeping reality steady. There were a countless number of these lines, seemingly infinite and everywhere.

Shin had long since grown used to this sight, after training his teleporting Ability for so long. It had become almost second nature to visualize these lines, and the real world under them, at the same time.

Now, however, as Shin looked around, he could see exactly what Micheal had been talking about.

‘Over there, everything is messed up… wait, what?!’ Shin’s thoughts stuttered to a halt as he stared at one particular location, where the lines of space were extraordinarily chaotic.

Sophia noticed his reaction and looked over at the same spot, nodding to herself.

‘There it is! The First Gate.’

Spread out around the entry platform that the duo had arrived out was a large room made up of finely carved grey stone. These stones each had various symbols and glyphs carved into them and gave off a very dim amount of light, the only light source in the room. The room stretched around 25 meters wide and was shaped like a large circle, expanding outward from the platform.

The only other irregularity in the room were the five large stone archways that were set in different parts along the wall.

The Five Gates.

Tallanoran’s Inheritance was something he created to prepare for the inevitable. The Soul King had seen the writing on the wall when it came to Toren aggression and had prepared his Inheritance to ensure his people survived. He also had intended to make it impossible for any creature that wasn’t a Dark Wraith to discover.

Unfortunately for the Soul King, the Toren Ascension into a Tribe of Deities was something that was completely beyond his expectations. By the time he realized how horrific the monsters that were called ‘Deities’ were, it was already too late.

He had managed to create his Inheritance, but instead of blocking it off from all except Dark Wraiths, the ancient legacy ground was left incomplete.

The Shadow Seekers that Sophia and Shin had previously killed were the key to open the Inheritance. Those phantoms were originally created by the Inheritance to act as both guards and guides for any Dark Wraiths that came within range, to lead them to this safe haven.

Because Tallanoran didn’t manage to finish his work before he perished, the Shadow Seekers only maintained their ‘guard’ function, attacking anyone, including Dark Wraiths, that came within range. Without anything to lead someone to the specific, hidden rock wall that was the opening to the Inheritance, the treasure ground remained unknown until now.

After Sophia and Shin killed their respective Shadow Seekers, the Inheritance viewed the ‘guide’ function that was never properly installed as activated, opening up access to the Inheritance for them. As long as they knew the location, which they learned from Micheal, they could just waltz on in.

Sophia walked down from the raised stone platform, descending down a small set of stairs, and walked over to the archway that had a symbol shaped like a circle with a dot in it on its front. The Shop translated all verbal languages, but when it came to written words, the function only worked for Earth-based languages. Still, she knew from Micheal that this symbol meant ‘First’ in the language of the Dark Wraiths.

“It’s just like Micheal said.” Shin muttered as he shook his head, once again bemused by Micheal’s ability to know things he shouldn’t.

“This is it, Shin.” Sophia turned to the lanky blond as he ambled down the stairs after her, her voice tinged with a hint of excitement and apprehension.

“Finally… We have a chance to catch up.” Sophia clenched her fists tightly as she looked at the towering stone edifice.

Belying his usual easygoing nature, Shin didn’t respond but stayed quiet as he looked at the Gate. Sophia’s words seemed to resound deep within him, causing the smile on his face to fade.

Dark Wraiths were a long-lived species. This particular facet had its advantages and its disadvantages. They would take a long time to grow strong, but when they did, they remained strong for a long, long time.

Tallanoran took that into account when he created the Five Gates of his Inheritance, his answer to that problem taking the form of the First Gate.

Two vague, shadowy figures began to morph into existence on top of the circular platform Shin and Sophia had arrived at. Clumps of dark essence pulsated in a growing circle as Shadow Seekers shaped like Shin and Sophia started to appear.

The duo glanced back at the creatures before turning their attention over towards the Gate.

“We only have one chance, Shin.” Sophia spoke steadily, forcing herself to calm down.

“I know.” Shin returned slowly.

Humans could challenge the Five Gates thanks to the incomplete safeguards on the Inheritance, but they could only try each Gate one time. After that, the Inheritance would recognize its mistake and block them from repeating that Gate.

Sophia turned to look at Shin. After a moment’s pause, she walked over and patted him on the shoulder.

“Don’t be too nervous. Just hold on for as long as you can.”

“Hey! I’m not nervous! Hold on for yourself, Soap Opera.” Shin gave her a half-hearted glare.

“Soap Opera?” Sophia raised an eyebrow.

“…it wasn’t my best.” Shin cracked a smile as he turned to look back at the stone archway, the levity fading away, replaced with nervousness.

The First Gate.

The Gate of Suffering.

A gateway that led to a special, imaginary landscape where you didn’t need to eat, you didn’t need to sleep, you didn’t need to do anything but train. You could unleash the full extent of your powers without worry about injury, expanding your comprehension of Concepts like Sword Mastery.

As for your training partner…

Sophia glanced back at the Shadow Seekers that were currently still forming.

They came along for free at the level of strength you raised them to, by killing them outside. And, unlike outside, once inside the First Gate, the Shadow Seekers would possess a growing level of sentience.

Fight. Train. Suffer. Repeat. Over and over.

Even if you died, you would merely reform inside the Gate, taking no actual injury.

The First Gate was a haven for anyone who wanted to train, and was actually the safest of the Five Gates, allowing you to leave whenever you wanted.

However... all these things paled in comparison to the most important factor of all.

Dark Wraiths took a long time to train... and the Soul King designed this Gate as a way to overcome that.

The moment you entered the Gate, your real body was stored in timeless stasis while your consciousness and Soul were projected into the imaginary landscape.

And in that landscape…

For every 3 minutes that passed in the real world…

An entire year would pass for the person inside the Gate.

.

Chapter 20



The rustle of leaves stirred the afternoon air, the warm sun beating down overhead through the leafy foliage.

Around half an hour had passed since Micheal departed with the Farians.

In that time, Micheal had met with the leaders of the party and discussed the specifics of the route they would take through the Dragon Mountains, chatting as they jogged toward the south. They had already met and talked about this before they left, but there was no harm in touching base again and making sure they were all on the same page.

Serena Kowalsi, the Disciple Apparent of the Wise Lady, kept to herself mostly during the meeting, apart from sending Micheal mixed, indecisive glares. She looked like she was trying to hide her feelings but did a terrible job, letting Micheal read her like an open book.

‘Hmm… It looks like she dislikes me but also feels grateful and therefore doesn’t know how to act.’ Micheal lightly smiled when he made that observation. After all the attacks on the Farians by the human Beasts of Providence, he knew it would be hard for some Farians to trust him, even after all he did.

The fact that Serena was making efforts to overcome that already said a lot for her character.

As for Shadow Captain Sprel and the two lieutenants he brought to the meeting as aides: Micheal found all three men to be incredibly professional, in a similar vein to professional military officers from back on Earth. Regardless of whether or not they liked Micheal, they were completing a mission and didn’t allow their emotions to get in the way.

‘It’s good and bad, I suppose.’ Their professionalism was a sign of loyalty, but also meant it would be impossible for Micheal to recruit them.

For, one of the first things Micheal did after he finished talking with the Farians was to activate his Eyes of the Deep to perform a Divine Scan on the two prominent Farian leaders that had joined him.

‘Do they have any potential?’ There was no way the two of them could have risen to the positions they held without exceptional Growth Ratings.

While he didn’t like the concept of judging someone’s worth based purely on their growth potential, Micheal knew it would be foolish to not take full advantage of an Ability that allowed him to see that. He needed to build up his own forces and it only made sense to put more focus and effort on allies that had great potential.

He scanned the Shadow Captain first, his eyes glimmering for the briefest of moments.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Grand Lional Farian

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: C+ (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

END: C (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

REG: B- (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower) SOUL: C- (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

MANA: C+ (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

Path Notes: A Grand Lional Farian that walks the Path of the Sword.

.

‘Hmm, that’s about what I expected.’ Micheal nodded to himself.

Shadow Captain Sprel had been a notable figure during the Great War, proving himself to be a behemoth of a warrior with balanced but powerful stats all around and exceptionally high regenerative capabilities.

After checking the numbers and grades, Micheal sighed to himself.

Sprel’s Growth Rates were exceptional. With balanced 'Rare' Growth Rates all around and an exceptional 'Heroic or lower' Regeneration Growth Rate, he would be a fearsome combatant even later down the line in the 7 Layers.

‘Unfortunately…’ He shook his head.

A Soul Growth Rate of 'Rare or lower' was a significant weakness, at least in Micheal’s eyes.

‘If more than one of his melee Stats were rated 'Heroic' and not 'Rare,' it might be different.’

Humans could change their Growth Rates extremely easily thanks to the plethora of Abilities they could purchase in the Shop. A human’s Growth Rate meant very little in the grand scheme of things.

For all other races, however… one’s Growth Rate was an inherent trait that was extraordinarily difficult for them to change. Without access to the Shop, Sprel would have to hunt down extremely rare items if he wanted to enhance his Growth Rates.

‘He’s a well-above average warrior, a powerful warrior, in fact. But…’ Micheal’s eyes took on a grim hue.

‘I don’t need powerful warriors...’

‘I need monsters.’

To challenge the Deities with anything less would merely invite a slaughter.

Micheal subtly turned his attention over to Serena, activating his Eyes of the Deep once more, without expecting anything much.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Red Phoenix Farian

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: D+ (Growth Rate: Rare or lower) END: D+ (Growth Rate: Rare or lower) REG: C (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower) SOUL: B- (Growth Rate: Mythical or higher) MANA: D+ (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower) Path Notes: A Red Phoenix Farian that nears the Path of the Original Flame.

.

‘What the-?!’ His non-existent expectations were blown away.

He regained control of his expression as he plastered on a calm facade, staring at the results of the Divine Scan with slightly widened eyes.

‘The Farians had a second person with a Mythical Rating?! And not just that, she has two Heroic Growth Ratings too!’ He was genuinely shocked.

The Lord Justiciar had a 'Mythical or higher' Growth Rating in STR, something that proved a major factor in why he was regarded as the strongest Farian of all time.

A Mythical Growth Rating in anything was extraordinarily rare, to the point that there were entire species in the 7 Layers that never had a single denizen appear with a 'Mythical or lower' Growth Rating throughout their entire history, let alone a 'Mythical or higher' Growth Rating.

‘Why haven’t I ever seen a genius like her in the first timeline?!’ Micheal’s thoughts raced ahead of him as he glanced at the pretty female Farian.

‘Wait a second… it says she’s a Red Phoenix Farian? The Path of the Original Flame? Serena Kowalsi?!’ Micheal’s perfect memories stirred as he thought backwards, sifting through the sands of time to the right moment.

In those memories, a single name appeared: Firestorm.

It was the nickname given to the Tribal Heir of the Kowalsi Tribe, a Farian Bloodline Flame Master. She was the first and last of her kind, a woman capable of using her Bloodline Magic to spawn enormous avalanches of fire that were capable of washing over entire battlefields, incinerating thousands of lives in a blazing instant. A living weapon of mass destruction.

In Micheal’s memories, Firestorm had been a heavily disfigured Farian with a face horribly marred by severe burns. She had a slightly hunched back and an incredibly vile temper, a woman that cackled madly with glee as she slaughtered other beings in droves.

She could not have looked more different than the woman before Micheal…

‘But it has to be her.’ The odds of another Farian with Growth Ratings like her appearing was nigh impossible.

In the first timeline, the Kowalsi Tribe that were said to be the strongest Farian Tribe had abandoned the other Farians to continue climbing the 7 Layers, most of them vanishing from the Second Layer. The Kowalsi had little impact on the Great War, save for their legendary Tribal Heir that stayed behind to fight.

‘She’s the Disciple Apparent of Myla Hannis… if she’s Firestorm, then in the first timeline, she must’ve been disfigured during the assassination of the Wise Lady.’ Micheal did the obvious math, drawing connections from the changes he’d made between the timelines.

The Vile King was meticulous. Without knowledge of his actions and capabilities, it would take a miracle to survive anything he put effort into, a miracle made possible by Serena’s abnormally high Growth Ratings and Bloodline.

Firestorm's real name had never been made public, but everything he saw pointed to her being Serena. In fact, now that he thought about it, both Myla and Firestorm were known to have shared the same Bloodline.

‘A Farian driven insane by rage and hatred, gifted with enormous potential and Bloodline Magic…’ His eyes widened.

It fit into place perfectly.

‘She’s Firestorm.’

‘...’

Micheal put his focus into his jogging while he settled his heart and mind down, forcing himself back down to a level of calm. Over the next part of his journey, as he and the Farians continued onward, he began to calculate and plan in his head, adjusting his plans for the future as best he could.

Finally, as he neared half a year into the 4th Wave, he had come across his next potential new recruit into his team.

‘Let’s not rush anything. Just because her Growth Ratings are high enough doesn’t mean she has the right mentality or attitude.’ He reminded himself to stay realistic.

High Growth Ratings meant nothing if the person holding them couldn’t take advantage of them, and, in the first place, there was no guarantee that he could convince her to join him.

‘For now, let’s focus on why I have them with me in the first place.’ He nodded to himself.

Before he went to obtain the essence of a Deity to activate his Title System and met back up with Shin and Sophia, there was a pit stop they had to make along the way.

A massive war growing closer and closer to breaking out on the Second Layer. With the Darmaton Plague ravaging the Byrens, humanity, and all the other races except the nigh-immune Farians, tensions were rising and people were angry.

The Six Lords of the Byrens were stirring up the various Martial Artist Sects and the other races, while the Vile King’s Beasts of Providence did the same for humanity.

Micheal couldn’t hope to compete with that level of manipulation and influence, no matter the future knowledge he held.

But he knew someone else that could.

‘The Nirvana Saint is dead?’ Micheal scoffed.

In the first timeline, even the Vile King himself couldn’t kill the Nirvana Saint.

The only one that managed that was the Titled Deity Navir, an unbelievably powerful regressor Deity that reigned over the Sixth Layer.

The Lord Justiciar had reached out to the Rakkonians.

The Orkals were already a lost cause, enslaved by the Byrens on the other side of the continent.

The Byrens were a party that would remain neutral as long as the Six Lords were handled.

All that was left was the humans.

Micheal’s eyes gleamed as he finally arrived at the entrance to the Dragon Mountains, his mind filled to the brim with countless thoughts and plans.

It was time to rally the resistance.

.

Chapter 21



Day slipped into night in the blink of an eye.

The rustling crackle of a burning fire echoed in the still air, painting the surrounding forest a warm hue of orange and yellow. The temperature of surrounding air was cool, a sign of the growing onset of winter.

Micheal’s eyes fluttered open as he exited his hours-long meditation, cycling the Ki energy in his body with a sigh of comfort. He smiled as he looked around at a small stone house, nodding to himself.

They had made excellent time.

After he and his group set off for the Dragon Mountains, they had taken no breaks until this exact moment. Micheal didn’t know whether it was luck or just a coincidence, but they didn’t come across even a hint of the undead Blue Drake that lived in this region.

The route they took through the Dragon Mountains was one exclusive to the Farians, a path Micheal hadn’t even heard of before.

According to Captain Sprel, one of the first things the Lord Justiciar had ordered when he arrived on the Second Layer was for several Farian Blood Masters to drill several secret tunnels all the way through the mountain range. They functioned both as a means of general transport as well as an escape route for the Farians if relations between them and the dominant Silent Sword Sect that ruled over this area should sour.

After blitzing across the entirety of the Dragon Mountains in a single afternoon, they had arrived on a small grassy plain that bordered a large forest. They ended up more than 60 miles to the east of Tansol Town and the Tansol Pass, the original route Micheal had taken to reach the Farians.

They also ended up only a couple hours north-west of Yvvtal’s Inheritance, or, at least, the rapidly transforming Magic Forest that had replaced it.

In the end, Micheal didn’t get to see the newly-born Magic Forest with his own eyes. Instead, they headed directly south until they reached their current location, a normal forest around a hundred miles south of the Dragon Mountains.

After sprinting for the entire day, even the superhuman elite Farian soldiers became exhausted. Before Micheal came to the Farians rescue, he would have been included in that tally as well.

However, thanks to his Heartflame Physique constantly absorbing energy as they ran, Micheal found himself settling into a rhythm that left him full of energy. He consistently regained the energy he spent as he ran, leaving him in equilibrium.

Micheal’s unique, evolved Physique overcame, to some extent, one of the major shortcomings of Micheal’s build: his lack of an even halfway decent Recovery stat.

Because Micheal focused the vast majority of his effort into growing only one of his melee stats, Strength, with a secondary focus on Endurance, his Recovery stat was pitifully low. Even mid-level warriors on the First Layer had a higher Recovery stat than him.

Of course, there was good reason for this. Why would he need a stat that centered around enhancing a creature’s natural regeneration when he could just cure all of his injuries by breaking a Life Orb? Any focus he put into this stat would be a waste.

If he wanted any chance of overcoming what was to come, he needed, among other things, to become as physically powerful as humanely possible.

The problem came from the fact that the Recovery stat didn’t solely refer to the regenerative powers of a being. It also affected one’s overall stamina.

A higher Recovery stat allowed a person to restore their body at a faster rate, which included replenishing one’s energy stores through absorbing latent energy in the air.

Of course, this was solely relegated to passive regeneration. No matter how high one’s Recovery stat, entering a meditative state would always work far faster when it came to recovering one’s energy.

However, that passive regeneration could have a sizable impact when it came to long-term battles of endurance or, as in the case of the present, long-term trials of stamina.

‘Well, it’s not like I didn’t know about that ahead of time.’ Micheal shrugged to himself as he stood up.

He was aware of the flaw in his growth, but he didn’t exactly have a choice.

He would never outlast a Deity in any form of extended combat, especially not against the strongest Deities.

In fights that would end in seconds at best, minutes at worst, passive regeneration wouldn’t matter.

‘Still, this is nice.’ Micheal grinned as he opened and closed his hand, feeling the warm energy flowing in his veins.

His Heartflame Physique seemed to make all of the energy he absorbed fill him with a sense of warmth and comfort. He had studied this feeling all throughout their journey, examining his body and the changes within it.

It wouldn’t enhance his ability to heal like a high Recovery stat would, but at least it resolved his problem of diminishing stamina.

Micheal’s gaze scanned around the campsite, a hint of appreciation filling his eyes.

In lieu of the basic tents or uncovered sleeping bags that Micheal had grown used to sleeping in while travelling, the Farians had constructed a miniature village in a matter of minutes to serve as their campground.

The detachment of warriors from the Shadow Guard had included a pair of Farians that possessed the Gorgar Lizard Bloodline, a Bloodline that allowed them to manipulate stone and rock at will. At first glance, it wasn’t a particularly powerful Bloodline given that they could only shift the earth around a meter per minute.

However, when it came to logistics like setting up camps, barricades, or fortifications, there was nothing better. They had created more than 3 dozen fortified stone houses in less than 15 minutes.

Micheal walked out through the front door of the hut they’d created for him, passing by several evenly dispersed fires that lit the camp up. While the mission they were on was secret, they themselves didn’t actually need to hide. A group their size was bound to be noticed, regardless of how they set up camp.

He spread his senses out around him as he walked, his powerful Soul stat letting him take in the presence of anything nearby.

Most of the Farians were asleep, save for the rotating night guard that kept watch on the area outside the camp, including below the ground, on the ground and above the ground. They had been lucky enough to avoid any dangerous Magic Beasts thus far, but there was no guarantee that would continue.

After a few seconds, Micheal frowned as he noticed something off.

‘Where’s Serena?’ He had memorized the energy signatures of everyone here, but didn’t find her among the slumbering Farians. It wasn’t impossible to hide one’s energy signature, but given that Micheal had the highest Soul stat of anyone present, it wasn’t easy to escape his notice.

He closed his eyes for a few moments, extending his senses to their absolute limit.

The crackling fire became intensified, raging like a storm ablaze. The rustle of leaves clashed like chaotic cannons while the cool breeze transformed into a loud, rippling river.

Micheal focused on these sounds, slowly isolating them away as he looked underneath.

The qualitative Master transformation he underwent gave him a much greater control of his body, to the point where isolating specific sounds was merely a matter of effort.

Soon, his senses tingled as he picked up the chirps of bugs, prowling forest creatures, and the shifting groans of plants drifting in the breeze.

Seconds passed as he sifted through the noise, maintaining an incredible level of concentration that could only be picked up after more than a decade of constant training and experience.

Finally, after roughly 30 seconds had passed, Micheal detected the breathing of a Farian that wasn’t within the confines of the camp.

‘Found you!’ Before he could continue that thought, however…

As Micheal’s senses zeroed in on her, he also felt the blood within his veins seem to resonate ever so slightly.

This shocked Micheal out of his deep concentration, bringing his eyes wide open as he stared down at his open palm.

“Huh.” He muttered quietly to himself.

The feeling was buried deep within his blood, a sensation of familiarity that he hadn’t noticed until he focused on Serena.

‘Does it have to do with my Physique?’ His instincts were telling him this was correct.

He pulled up the description of his Physique.

.

—- Heartflame Physique - 3 Stars —-

A Physique that contains a hint of the essence of a Phoenix. From life unto death and death unto life. This 3 Star Heartflame Physique vastly enhances the host's ability to absorb latent energy in the air. Excess energy will be absorbed into and empower the flesh. Greatly enhances resistance to curses, mental attacks, and spiritual attacks.

.

‘The essence of a Phoenix…’ He nodded to himself. Serena possessed the Red Phoenix Bloodline. Perhaps all Phoenixes were inherently able to recognize each other? While neither of them had a pure Phoenix Bloodline, it was enough to create a feeling of familiarity.

Micheal made mental note of that as he began to walk in Serena’s direction.

They were only one day into their journey, but he could already tell that if he didn’t do anything, Myla’s Disciple Apparent would doubtlessly avoid talking to him the entire trip.

‘I’m not going to let a Mythical talent slip through my hands without even trying.’ Micheal waved at a Farian sentry as he left the campsite, his eyes gazing out into the darkness.

Even if she didn’t like him, she’d at least hear him out if he started a conversation right?

…

Well, maybe.

‘Alright… first things first… how do I open? I can’t just start by talking about the weather right…? Hmm…’ Micheal’s mind grew clouded as he headed over towards Serena’s location.

‘This might be harder than I thought…’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Serena let out a frustrated sigh as she stared at the smoky pile of wood she had cobbled together.

‘Why won’t it work?!’

She glared at the wood again with a frown.

She was currently standing several dozens of meters away from the main camp, practicing late into the night. Her long brown hair was tied up in a bun and she had changed into a set of tight black pants, boots, and a form fitting grey shirt that clung to her, a set of enchanted clothes that were almost completely immune to fire.

‘Let’s try again.’

Serena’s grey eyes lit up as she activated her Bloodline.

Dull, orange flames burst into existence, covering the stack of wood in an instant. These flames danced all over the wood and began to flutter up into the air, simmering quietly.

Serena bit her lip as she stared at the crackling fire for one long moment.

The flames were orange and yellow… not red.

‘What am I doing wrong?!’

Serena possessed the Red Phoenix Bloodline, a Bloodline that was infamously powerful.

Farian Bloodlines were not like normal human bloodlines. They were a mystical, cosmic power, allowing Farians to draw and evolve into Bloodlines that were based off mythical beings. The Red Phoenix was an example of that. A powerful, legendary bird of flame that possessed unstoppable might.

Red Phoenix Bloodline users gained a portion of that strength in the form of the ability to create ‘Phoenix Fire.’

Phoenix Fire was a special type of fire that, offensively, had the power to burn almost endlessly, even if left to its own devices. These flames were extremely difficult to extinguish and capable of wearing down a stronger enemy’s stamina over time.

That very fire could be used to mark someone, transforming their life into a living hell as it constantly pulsated. Not only would it bring forth unending pain, it could also continue to spread if one didn’t pay careful attention, requiring continuous suppression through something like Ki, Mana, Divine Energy, or any other form of energy. The deadly fire could even ruin Artifacts, burning anything from swords to sandals and everything in-between. Spatial Rings weren't safe, the fire capable of spreading into and destroying a ring from the inside out if someone tried to store it.

Serena had heard of the horrors of Phoenix Fire from Myla herself. Warriors affected by it were forced to cut off fingers, hands, and even arms or legs in order to get rid of the ever-burning flame.

Leaving it on was a death sentence, regardless of how strong someone was. Superhumans still needed to sleep, or to at least observe periods of peaceful meditation, in order to survive. One could only go so many days without rest before they either perished or went insane and then perished.

When she successfully absorbed the Record Book, back during the horrifying assassination attempt that almost left Myla dead, Serena had gained real memories of Myla’s experience using Phoenix Fire.

Despite all of that, however…

She couldn’t bring out pure red Phoenix Fire.

‘I can remember teacher’s exact feelings and thoughts when she spawned Phoenix Fire. I’m doing everything the same!’ Myla’s eyes narrowed as she glared for the second time at the pile of burning wood.

‘...I just don’t understand…’ Her thoughts trailed off.

According to her teacher, Serena possessed a unique talent to draw upon her Bloodline near endlessly. The Wise Lady had personally taken Serena in and taught her how to unleash her flames, alongside all the training and history that went into becoming the Disciple Apparent of a Wise Lady.

If she could just master the ability to create Phoenix Fire in its purest form, she knew she’d be capable of unleashing enormous swathes of it. She would become a real, viable asset that could stand independent of her Tribe.

Serena let out a quiet sigh as she rubbed her eyes.

“Why is it so hard to understand...”

Just as she was about to start again, she heard the sound of crunching leaves coming from off to the side...

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“Who’s there?” A delicate, female voice echoed in the air as Micheal announced his presence by loudly walking on leaves, a voice that somehow sounded both confident and surprised at the same time.

“It’s just me, Micheal.” Micheal walked into the small, open clearing where Serena had been practicing, giving the Farian a friendly smile.

After discovering Serena’s location, Micheal had moved silently to her location. He had found her in the midst of her training and opted to wait for a moment when she took a break.

Inadvertently, he also overheard her complaints as she practiced and, out of his own personal experience, felt he had a good idea what her problem was.

Serena glanced at Micheal quietly, a conflicted look appearing and then vanishing from her face as she nodded at him.

“Can I help you?” While she didn’t trust humans as a whole, she felt that at least the one before her had done enough to prove himself trustworthy. There was little need to be on guard against him.

“Actually, I thought I might be able to help you.” Micheal returned with a nod of his own.

Serena quirked an eyebrow.

“Well, I’ll explain.” Micheal chuckled as he continued,

“I came this way because I felt a certain resonance between my Physique and your Bloodline, the first time I’d ever felt that.” Micheal pointed at his body and then waved over at her.

Serena nodded.

“When we were rescuing you, my teacher drew on her Bloodline to help heal you. We share the same Bloodline.” Serena had been there and witnessed firsthand the transformation that Micheal’s body went through, even if she didn’t quite understand the reasons for it. Humans were weird.

“I didn’t mean to intrude, but on the way, I couldn’t help but overhear some of the complaints you were raising.”

“Ah.” Serena blushed slightly as she awkwardly raised a hand to tug at her bun.

“Well, that…” She trailed off, unable to come up with an excuse.

“It’s natural to get frustrated.” Micheal shook his head as he slowly raised his right hand.

“I know what you’re going through.” Abruptly, the bright glow of Advanced Tier Sword Energy burst into existence as Micheal carefully drew the energy around his palm.

Serena stared at his palm, her eyes creasing.

“My Phoenix Fire is nothing like your Sword Energy.” She recognized the glowing source of energy from seeing other Farians wield it.

Micheal nodded.

“That’s true but also not true.” Micheal waved his hand off to the side in a sharp, cutting motion.

For a split second, the Advanced Tier Sword Energy was replaced by Master Tier Sword Energy. Micheal could only do this for a tiny moment and could only imbue just the tiniest amount without ripping his hand apart, but for a demonstration, it was more than enough.

The Golden Master Tier Sword Energy shot out and sliced through a falling leaf, perfectly splitting it in half.

“You’re a Master?!” Serena visibly started, her eyes widening as she stared at Micheal in shock.

The Master Tier was a state of being universally recognized by most species. The feeling of Master Tier Energy, whether that be Sword Energy, Ax Energy, or any other form of Weapon Energy, was a universal, golden color that emanated danger. This tier of Mastery wasn’t only limited to conceptual Weapon Energies either. One could achieve a Master Tier transformation in any of the endless ‘Paths’ one might take.

The fact that Micheal was a Master was not common knowledge. In fact, the only people that were aware of it for certain among the Farians were the Lord Justiciar and the Wise Lady.

Serena sputtered as she looked at Micheal, at a loss.

The fact that a human that looked to be her age was already a Master was indeed shocking.

After a couple of seconds, she pursed her lips as she asked, “Are you one of those Masters who revert back to their youth after transforming?” The Master Tier transformation was different for each person, but for most Weapon Energy Masters, the transformation came with the added benefit of extending their lifespan which sometimes included making the old appear youthful.

Micheal shook his head.

“No, I’m 18 years old, 19 in a couple months..” Technically, in mental years, he was more than 30 years old after returning to the past, but that didn’t affect his physical age.

Serena’s eyes took on a hint of appreciation and guarded respect.

Micheal mentally shrugged as he saw this, realizing the misunderstanding she was having.

‘Well, it doesn’t hurt my cause if she thinks I’m a sword wielding genius.’

“The reason I brought this up is because it relates to the problem you’re having.” Micheal continued.

“How so?” Serena’s stance became much more open to Micheal after discovering he was a Master.

“You’re trying to advance your Phoenix Fire to a higher state, right?” Micheal asked.

Serena nodded.

Micheal’s eyes flashed as he pulled up a Divine Scan of Serena.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Red Phoenix Farian

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: D+ (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

END: D+ (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

REG: C (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower)

SOUL: B- (Growth Rate: Mythical or higher)

MANA: D+ (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower)

Path Notes: A Red Phoenix Farian that nears the Path of the Original Flame.

.

He focused on the Path Notes of the Scan.

‘A Red Phoenix Farian that nears the Path of the Original Flame.’ His mind raced ahead of him as he read that.

The fact that it said she ‘nears’ the Path of the Original Flame instead of saying she ‘walked’ the Path of the Original Flame was significant. It meant she was on the cusp of comprehending how to use her Phoenix Flame, but had yet to fully reach that point.

“That’s exactly where the problem you’re having is.” Micheal motioned towards the still smoking pile of wooden debris.

“It’s a problem I’ve run into in the past, personally, as I tried to increase my Mastery over Sword Energy.” Micheal continued, his voice taking on a hint of confident finality.

“You’re trying to force Enlightenment.”

Perhaps more than anyone else, Micheal knew the deep, rage-inducing struggle of trying to force Enlightenment, Comprehension, or any of the other terms people used for when one enhanced their ability to manipulate a conceptual power.

He had struggled with this issue often, and repeatedly, during the first timeline, as someone whose talent for comprehending conceptual powers was mediocre.

It was a difficult thing to wrap one’s head around. The mystical energies that melded into the background of existence were a nigh-incomprehensible thing to most people, especially to the humans that came from Earth, a world where nothing of the sort existed.

Serena’s Phoenix Fire had its roots within the Path of the Original Flame, a Path Micheal was unfamiliar with, but something that, at its core, was a conceptual power, just like Sword Energy.

Serena bit her lips as she heard Micheal’s explanation, her face turning dour.

It was almost the exact response she had received from her teacher when she asked the Wise Lady about her problem.

“I know that I can’t force myself to grow… but what am I supposed to do?! I can’t just do nothing!” Serena clenched her fist.

She had seen far too many of the people she knew perish. Serena had arrived on the First Layer as a member of the Second Wave and had spent more than 2 years in the 7 Layers. Over the course of that time, a feeling of helplessness and impotence had risen within her.

She knew she possessed one of the most powerful Bloodlines among her people. Despite that, she had been stuck at the final step of evolution, unable to make full use of her Bloodline. If she could just cross this one final gap, her ability to attack, defend, and heal would increase enormously.

“At times like this, there’s only one thing you can do.” Micheal returned, his voice slow and steady.

“And what’s that?” Serena responded sharp and bitter.

“You need to relax and let it go.”

Serena’s eyes bulged for a moment as she heard Micheal’s solution, staring at him in disbelief.

Micheal smiled slightly and gave a helpless shrug.

“I know it sounds counterintuitive… but that’s what you need to do.”

Serena looked at him doubtfully.

"Are you saying I need to give up in order to improve?” She frowned, clearly unwilling to believe him.

Micheal paused for a moment as he stared at her, thinking for a few moments before making a decision.

“Well… it's not easy to explain. Here, if I can’t convince you with just that, why don’t I share with you my own, personal experience.” Micheal looked down at his hands for a moment, the smile on his face fading away.

“Let me tell you about the time I broke through to become a Master. Perhaps it will help.”

Serena’s frown eased up as she nodded her assent.

And like that, Micheal began to talk, changing certain details here and there to avoid exposing the fact that he had gone back in time.

His mind jumped back to the past, memories swarming up as he spoke…

Memories of the first timeline where, on the Third Layer, Micheal first broke through to the Master Tier.

.
